Euphonium spots + Byodoin + matcha · D9 Nara deer + Todaiji · D10 Osaka Dotonbori food · D11 Kobe beef + Arima Onsen · D12 fly KIX→New Chitose · D13 Otaru + Sapporo · D14 Sapporo, fly out. Or stop at D11 and fly home from Kansai (KIX).
why: Gives temples, food and one anime pilgrimage (Euphonium) with no long drives, and still ends in snowy Hokkaido if they want.
cost: transport approx. ¥35,000–55,000 pp (Tokyo→Kyoto Shinkansen ~¥14,200, local trains ~¥10,000, KIX→Chitose LCC ~¥8,000–20,000). Flight change: open-jaw, arrive Narita, leave from KIX (or CTS if the Hokkaido tail is kept). Loses Zao/Niseko skiing.
winterNote: Kyoto city gets settled snow only on a few days per winter (need 3–5 cm after a cold wave; go at opening time). Plan for cold, clear weather; snow is a bonus.
anime: Hibike! Euphonium (Uji Bridge, Daikichiyama lookout, Uji Shrine)

experience.hook: Golden temples, deer that bow, and the river town of Hibike! Euphonium.
moments: Walk up through thousands of orange torii gates at Fushimi Inari as the lanterns come on at dusk.
Stand at the Kinkaku-ji pond at opening time and see the gold pavilion, maybe with snow on its roof.
Climb to Uji's Daikichiyama lookout where Kumiko and Reina watched the town lights, then sip matcha by Uji Bridge.
Bow to the deer in Nara Park, feed them shika senbei, then face the huge bronze Buddha inside Todai-ji.
Eat hot takoyaki and kushikatsu under the Glico running-man sign in Dotonbori, then soak in Arima's rust-red gold water.
experience.tip: Check the Kyoto snow forecast the night before. If snow falls, be at the Kinkaku-ji gate for 9:00 opening, before it melts.

title: Tokaido slow road to Nagoya
titleJa: 東海道 ゆっくり西へ（箱根・静岡・浜松・名古屋）
summary: Go west from Tokyo in 5 days, one stop per day, and send big suitcases ahead to Nagoya. D5 Sat Jan 23 Romancecar Shinjuku → Hakone-Yumoto, Hakone loop, ryokan night · D6 Sun Jan 24 Moto-Hakone → Tokai Bus → Mishima Skywalk (Fuji view) → Kodama to Shizuoka (24 min), Hobby Square, night Shizuoka · D7 Mon Jan 25 bus to Nihondaira, ropeway to Kunozan Toshogu, Hikari to Hamamatsu (20 min), Kanzanji ropeway over Lake Hamana, onsen night at Kanzanji · D8 Tue Jan 26 Yamaha Communication Plaza (Iwata) or Hamamatsu unagi lunch, Hikari to Nagoya (30 min), Toyota Commemorative Museum, Osu and miso katsu · D9 Wed Jan 27 Ghibli Park or SCMaglev and Railway Park, then on to Kyoto/Osaka in the evening. Train cost Tokyo → Nagoya this way is about ¥19,000–22,000 per person, against ¥11,100 for a direct Nozomi.
why: It turns the Tokyo–Osaka move into five small trips with Fuji, onsen, cars and Ghibli, and no day has more than 1 h 30 min on trains.
cost: Trains/buses about ¥19,000–22,000 pp (Hakone Freepass Odawara ¥6,000 + Odakyu Shinjuku–Odawara ¥910 + Romancecar ¥1,200; Mishima→Shizuoka Kodama ¥1,980 unreserved; Shizuoka→Hamamatsu Hikari ¥2,330 unreserved; Hamamatsu→Nagoya Hikari ¥4,840 reserved; local buses). Hotels: 1 ryokan + 3 business hotels.
winterNote: New route days 5–9. Weekday traps: Hobby Square, Suzuki museum and Toyota Commemorative Museum close on Mondays; Ghibli Park and SCMaglev park close on Tuesdays (Jan 26 closed); Toyota Kaikan closes Sundays. No snow on this coast; Hakone roads can ice in the morning. Fares from Jorudan for Jan 25, 2027.

places.ja: 日本平ロープウェイ 日本平駅
かんざんじロープウェイ

experience.hook: Five short hops west, each with Fuji, a hot bath or cars.
moments: Ride the Romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto and soak in a ryokan bath the first night.
Walk Mishima Skywalk, Japan's longest footbridge, with Mt Fuji straight ahead on a clear morning.
Float 5 minutes down the Nihondaira ropeway to the red and gold Kunozan Toshogu shrine.
Cross Lake Hamana on Japan's only ropeway over a lake, then soak at Kanzanji Onsen.
End in Nagoya with miso katsu in Osu and a Ghibli Park day.
experience.tip: Send big suitcases from the Tokyo hotel to the Nagoya hotel (¥3,020 per 160-size bag) and travel five days with daypacks.

title: Two-day Tokaido: Shizuoka, Hamamatsu, Nagoya
titleJa: 東海道 2日間（静岡・浜松・名古屋）
summary: A fast version of the westward move that uses the weekend. D5 Sat Jan 23 Hikari Tokyo → Shizuoka (59 min, ¥6,270 reserved), Nihondaira and Kunozan ropeway, Hobby Square, Hikari to Hamamatsu (20 min), unagi dinner · D6 Sun Jan 24 Suzuki Museum at 9:00 (weekend = full hours), Hikari to Nagoya (30 min), SCMaglev and Railway Park or Toyota Commemorative Museum, Osu and miso katsu at night. D7 continue to Kyoto/Osaka (Nagoya → Shin-Osaka 50 min, ¥6,270–6,480).
why: Pegasis and Aoki see Fuji country, two car museums and a Shinkansen simulator but lose only one day against a direct train.
cost: Trains ≈ ¥13,400 pp (Tokyo→Shizuoka ¥6,270 + Shizuoka→Hamamatsu ¥2,330 + Hamamatsu→Nagoya ¥4,840) + buses/ropeway ≈ ¥2,700 + museums ¥1,000–1,200
winterNote: New route days 5–6. Suzuki Museum: free, booking needed; on weekdays Sep–Jan visitors enter only after 15:00 (school groups), so the Sunday slot matters. Nihondaira ropeway has a planned stop Dec 1–21, 2026 only. Fares from Jorudan (Jan 2027 dates).

experience.hook: Fuji views, a shrine by ropeway, then Suzuki and bullet trains.
moments: Stand on the Nihondaira hilltop and look across Suruga Bay to snowy Mt Fuji.
Eat grilled unagi in Hamamatsu, the eel town of Lake Hamana.
Walk the Suzuki Museum from the 1909 loom to Jimny and Hayabusa bikes.
Drive the N700 Shinkansen simulator at SCMaglev and Railway Park in Nagoya.
Finish with a huge miso katsu in Osu.
experience.tip: Book the Suzuki Museum online (free) for Sunday morning; weekday visits in January start only at 15:00.

title: Hakone as first stop, no suitcases
titleJa: 箱根を西行きの最初の宿に（手ぶら観光）
summary: Make Hakone the first night of the westward trip instead of a day trip from Tokyo. Take the Romancecar to Hakone-Yumoto, hand bags to the station luggage counter, loop Hakone with the Freepass, then leave west by Tokai Bus from Moto-Hakone to Mishima (via Mishima Skywalk) or by Tozan train to Odawara and the Shinkansen.
why: It saves the trip back to Tokyo and gives one ryokan onsen night before the business hotels start.
cost: Freepass (Hakone area, from Odawara) 2 days ¥6,000 + Odakyu Shinjuku–Odawara ¥910 + Romancecar ¥1,200; luggage ¥1,500 per bag each way; ryokan extra
winterNote: New route days 5–6. Luggage counter at Hakone-Yumoto: drop 8:30–12:00, bags at hotel after 15:00; return trip must be booked at the hotel desk by 10:00, pick up at Yumoto 13:30–18:30, and it only goes back to Yumoto. Snow can stop delivery. Ropeway and boats stop in strong wind.

places.ja: 箱根湯本駅 手荷物配送カウンター

experience.hook: Arrive in Hakone with empty hands, leave west over Mishima Skywalk.
moments: Sit in the Romancecar from Shinjuku and watch the hills rise after Odawara.
Hand your suitcases to the counter at Hakone-Yumoto and walk off with only a daypack.
Loop Hakone: Tozan train switchbacks, ropeway over Owakudani steam, pirate boat on Lake Ashi.
Soak in the ryokan bath at night while the air outside is near 0 °C.
Take the morning bus from Moto-Hakone to Mishima Skywalk for Fuji across the bridge.
experience.tip: If you leave west via Mishima, the station service cannot follow you; send bags by Yamato from the ryokan to your next hotel.

title: Atami early cherry blossoms at night
titleJa: あたみ桜 糸川桜まつり・熱海温泉泊
summary: Stop one night in Atami, the seaside onsen town 36 min from Tokyo by Hikari. The Itokawa river walk has 'Atami-zakura', Japan's earliest cherry blossoms, lit up every night during the January festival; then soak in a hotel onsen above the bay.
why: Real cherry blossoms in January, plus an onsen night by the sea, on the direct line west.
cost: Tokyo→Atami Hikari ¥4,070 reserved; Atami→Shizuoka Kodama ¥3,100; festival free; onsen hotel extra
winterNote: New route day 5. 2026 festival: Jan 10–Feb 8, light-up daily 16:30–23:00, weekend free sakura tea; 2027 not announced, likely similar. Kawazu cherry festival is later (2026: Feb 7–Mar 8). No Atami fireworks in late Jan (next: Feb 21, 2027). The existing Atami plum idea covers the plum garden.

places.ja: 糸川遊歩道 ドラゴン橋

experience.hook: Pink cherry blossoms in January, lit over a small river by the sea.
moments: Walk down from Atami Station through the covered shopping street toward the sea.
Stroll the Itokawa river walk under pink Atami-zakura, lit after 16:30.
Stand on Dragon Bridge and photograph blossoms against the neon of the old onsen town.
Soak in your hotel's hot spring bath with the dark sea below.
experience.tip: Come on a weekend morning for free sakura tea, then return after dark for the light-up.

title: Shuzenji onsen night in Izu
titleJa: 修善寺温泉
summary: A quiet, old onsen town in the middle of Izu, 37 min from Mishima by the local Sunzu Line. Walk the bamboo forest path and the river with Tokko-no-yu, stay in a ryokan, and come back to Mishima for the Shinkansen west.
why: A more traditional onsen night than Hakone, easy to add between Hakone/Mishima and Shizuoka.
cost: Mishima→Shuzenji ¥550 each way (Atami→Shuzenji direct Odoriko ¥1,840); ryokan with 2 meals often ¥15,000–30,000 pp (check)
winterNote: New route days 5–6. Mild, no snow. Tokko-no-yu is now for viewing only (no bathing). Kawazu cherry blossoms (further south) start in February, after this trip.

experience.hook: A river, a bamboo path and a ryokan in the middle of Izu.
moments: Ride the small Sunzu Line train from Mishima past fields and Fuji views.
Walk the bamboo forest path along the Katsura river as lanterns come on.
See Tokko-no-yu, the spring said to be opened by the monk Kukai.
Eat a ryokan dinner of Izu seafood and soak in the bath before bed.
experience.tip: Walk the bamboo path early in the morning before day-trip buses arrive.

title: Numazu port seafood and deep-sea aquarium
titleJa: 沼津港・沼津港深海水族館
summary: Stop at Numazu port on the way west: eat a fresh aji (horse mackerel) or seafood bowl at the port restaurants, then see the Deep Sea Aquarium with frozen coelacanths. Until Jan 31, 2027 it has a 'Godzilla Minus Zero' collab with Godzilla figures and design material.
why: Seafood lunch plus a Godzilla show fits a Hakone → Mishima → Shizuoka day, and adds to the Love Live stop if they want it.
cost: Aquarium adult ¥2,200; seafood bowl about ¥1,500–3,000 (check); Mishima→Numazu local ¥200s
winterNote: New route day 6. Godzilla −0.0 collab: Oct 3, 2026 – Jan 31, 2027 (stickers for the first 25,000 visitors from Dec 1). Aquarium 10:00–18:00 (hours change by season). The existing Numazu Love Live idea covers Uchiura and Aqours spots.

experience.hook: Frozen coelacanths and Godzilla, next to Japan's deepest bay.
moments: Eat a fresh aji or shirasu bowl at a port restaurant by the fish market.
Stand in front of the two frozen coelacanths, the only ones shown in the world.
Look at Godzilla figures from each era in the Godzilla Minus Zero collab rooms.
Watch giant Japanese spider crabs from Suruga Bay walk in the tanks.
experience.tip: Go before Jan 31, 2027; after that the Godzilla collab ends.

title: Nihondaira Fuji view and Kunozan ropeway
titleJa: 日本平・日本平ロープウェイ・久能山東照宮
summary: From Shizuoka Station take the bus to the Nihondaira hilltop for a wide Fuji and Suruga Bay view, then ride the 5-min ropeway down to Kunozan Toshogu, the first shrine of Tokugawa Ieyasu. Back in town, the free Shizuoka Hobby Square (Tamiya, Bandai, Hasegawa) is 1 min from the station.
why: The best Fuji view on the Tokaido line, a national treasure shrine, and Shizuoka's model-kit culture for anime and car fans.
cost: Bus Shizuoka Sta→Nihondaira ¥710 one way; ropeway round trip ¥1,250; shrine admission extra (check); Hobby Square free
winterNote: New route days 6–7. Winter air gives the clearest Fuji. Ropeway daily, Nihondaira dep. 9:10–16:45; planned stop Dec 1–21, 2026 only. Hobby Square 11:00–18:00 weekdays, 10:00–18:00 weekends, closed Mondays. The life-size Gundam stood in Shizuoka only in 2010–2011; there is no statue now.

places.ja: 日本平ロープウェイ 日本平駅
エスパルスドリームプラザ

experience.hook: Fuji over the bay, then a cable car down to a golden shrine.
moments: Look from Nihondaira Yume Terrace across Suruga Bay and Miho pine beach to snowy Fuji.
Ride the 5-minute ropeway over the deep Byobu valley to Kunozan.
Walk up to the lacquered red-and-gold shrine where Ieyasu was first buried.
Browse new plastic kits from Tamiya and Bandai at Hobby Square, and build one in the free workshop room.
experience.tip: Go up in the morning; Fuji often hides in clouds after noon. Hobby Square is closed Mondays.

title: Lake Hamana ropeway, oysters and unagi
titleJa: 浜名湖・かんざんじロープウェイ・舘山寺温泉
summary: Stay a night at Kanzanji Onsen on Lake Hamana, 45 min by bus from Hamamatsu Station. Ride Japan's only ropeway that crosses a lake, then eat winter lake food: unagi, Hamamatsu gyoza and the local 'kaki kaba-don' (grilled oyster bowl).
why: Eel, oysters and a salty onsen by a lake: a food night between Shizuoka and Nagoya with Fuji on clear days.
cost: Bus Hamamatsu Sta→Kanzanji about 45 min (fare check); ropeway round trip ¥1,300 (¥1,700 with music-box museum); unagi meal about ¥4,000–6,000 (check)
winterNote: New route day 7. Ropeway 10:00–17:30 in normal season; check the operating calendar. Oyster kaba-don and wild tora-fugu are winter dishes here. Pal Pal amusement park has its own winter days.

places.ja: かんざんじロープウェイ

experience.hook: A ropeway over the lake, eel for lunch, oysters for dinner.
moments: Ride the Kanzanji ropeway across Lake Hamana to Okusayama and look around 360 degrees.
Eat unagi-don in Hamamatsu, Japan's best-known eel town.
Try kaki kaba-don, Lake Hamana oysters grilled in sweet eel sauce, a winter dish.
Soak in Kanzanji's salty hot spring with the lake outside the window.
experience.tip: Look for Fuji from the Okusayama top on cold, clear mornings. Order Hamamatsu gyoza with bean sprouts as a side.

title: SCMaglev and Railway Park, Nagoya
titleJa: リニア・鉄道館
summary: JR Central's train museum by Nagoya port: 39 real trains, from steam engines to Shinkansen and the maglev test car, plus Japan's largest railway diorama. Try the N700 Shinkansen driving simulator.
why: After riding the Shinkansen west, they can drive one in the simulator and see the record-breaking maglev.
cost: Adult ¥1,200; N700 simulator ¥500 (first come, limited); Aonami Line Nagoya→Kinjo-futo ¥360, 24 min
winterNote: New route day 9 (or any day but Tuesday). 10:00–17:30, last entry 17:00, closed Tuesdays (Jan 19, 26, Feb 2). Simulator tickets sell out; on busy days they hand out numbered tickets before opening.

experience.hook: Drive a Shinkansen, then stand beside the maglev test car.
moments: Walk into the main hall past a steam engine, a Shinkansen and the maglev test car side by side.
Buy a ticket at the info desk and drive the N700 simulator for 15 minutes.
Watch the huge diorama run from day to night with trains and city lights.
Sit inside old Shinkansen cars and compare seats from each era.
experience.tip: Be at the door at 10:00 and go straight to the info desk for N700 simulator tickets.

title: Ghibli Park in winter
titleJa: ジブリパーク
summary: Studio Ghibli's park in Expo 2005 Aichi Commemorative Park, about 1 h from Nagoya. The Premium pass opens all five areas: Grand Warehouse, Hill of Youth, Dondoko Forest (Satsuki and Mei's house), Mononoke Village and Valley of Witches.
why: The biggest anime place on the Tokaido route, and it fits the Nagoya stop.
cost: O-sanpo Day Pass Premium ¥7,300 weekdays / ¥7,800 weekends; Standard (3 areas) ¥3,300 / ¥3,800; bus Nagoya Sta→park ¥1,200 or subway + Linimo
winterNote: New route day 9. Jan 2027 calendar: closed Tuesdays (Jan 19, Jan 26, Feb 2); weekday hours 10:00–17:00, weekends 9:00–17:00. Tickets only by advance booking (Lawson Ticket or Klook, passport check); they go on sale 2 months ahead on the 10th at 14:00 JST, so January 2027 opens Nov 10, 2026. No refunds.
anime: Studio Ghibli: My Neighbor Totoro (Satsuki and Mei's house), Princess Mononoke, Kiki's Delivery Service, Howl's Moving Castle

experience.hook: Walk into Totoro's house and Kiki's town in the same day.
moments: Enter the Grand Warehouse at your time slot and find famous Ghibli film scenes built full size.
Step inside Satsuki and Mei's house in Dondoko Forest and look into every room.
Walk the Valley of Witches past Howl's castle and Kiki's bakery.
Warm up with hot food at the Valley of Witches stalls on a cold winter afternoon.
experience.tip: Set an alarm for Nov 10, 2026, 14:00 Japan time; Premium weekday tickets for late January can go fast.

title: Nagoya food, Osu and the castle
titleJa: 名古屋めし・大須商店街・名古屋城
summary: One Nagoya day for its own food: hitsumabushi (eel on rice, eaten 3 ways) at Atsuta Horaiken near Atsuta Shrine, miso katsu at Yabaton's main shop in Osu, and spicy tebasaki wings at night. Walk Osu Kannon and the Osu shopping streets, and see Nagoya Castle's rebuilt Honmaru Palace.
why: Three famous local dishes in one day, plus Osu's anime, figure and used-goods shops.
cost: Hitsumabushi ¥4,950 (Horaiken main shop); miso katsu about ¥1,500–2,500 (check); castle ¥500
winterNote: New route days 8–9. Horaiken main shop closed Wednesdays and 2nd/4th Thursdays; Jingu branch closed Tuesdays and 2nd/4th Mondays (Jan 25, 26 both closed); Matsuzakaya branch closed Tuesdays. Yabaton Yabacho main shop 11:00–21:00, no closed day. Castle 9:00–16:30, main keep closed for rebuilding; Honmaru Palace open.

places.ja: あつた蓬莱軒 本店

experience.hook: Eel three ways, a pork cutlet in red miso, and wings at midnight.
moments: Eat hitsumabushi at Atsuta Horaiken: plain first, then with wasabi and leeks, then with hot dashi.
Walk Atsuta Shrine's cedar paths, home of one of Japan's three sacred treasures.
Order waraji tonkatsu at Yabaton in Osu, a plate-sized cutlet under sweet red miso.
Dig through anime goods, figures and retro games along the Osu shopping arcades.
End with peppery tebasaki chicken wings and a beer at an izakaya.
experience.tip: Line up at Horaiken 20 minutes before 11:30 opening; check which branch is open that weekday.

title: West via Alps: ice, thatch, crab
titleJa: 松本・高山・白川郷・奥飛騨・金沢→京都/大阪
summary: D5 (Sat Jan 23) Azusa Shinjuku→Matsumoto (2 h 39, ¥6,730); castle, Nawate street, castle projection mapping 18:00–22:00, ice-carving contest runs through the night · D6 (Sun Jan 24) see the finished ice sculptures at dawn, bus 9:55 Matsumoto→Takayama (arr. 12:28, ¥4,400, reserve), Sanmachi lunch, Nohi light-up tour Course B 15:10–20:45 to Shirakawa-go (¥16,000, deck ticket) · D7 (Mon) Miyagawa morning market 8:00, bus to Shinhotaka Ropeway (2,156 m snow deck), Hirayu no Mori onsen, back to Takayama; Hida no Sato light-up 17:30–20:30 · D8 (Tue) Nohi bus Takayama→Kanazawa (¥4,200, about 2 h 15), Higashi Chaya, 21st Century Museum, Omicho dinner · D9 (Wed) Kenrokuen free early entry 6:00–7:45 with snow ropes, Omicho crab brunch, afternoon Tsurugi + Thunderbird to Kyoto (2 h 04, ¥7,720) or Osaka (2 h 31, ¥9,410) · D10 (Thu) Kyoto/Osaka, fly to Hokkaido from Itami that evening or D11.
why: It gives both travellers a new snow scene every day (ice art, a lit-up snow village, a 2,000 m ropeway, a snow garden) and ends near Itami/KIX for the Hokkaido flight.
cost: Transport approx ¥32,000 pp (Azusa 6,730 + bus 4,400 + Okuhida 2-day bus/ropeway pass 7,700 + bus 4,200 + Kanazawa→Osaka 9,410) + Shirakawa-go tour ¥16,000 + Hida no Sato ¥300 + Kenrokuen ¥0 early / ¥320
winterNote: New route days 5–10. Shirakawa-go light-up is Sun Jan 24, 2027 (D6), 17:30–19:30, tickets only: Nohi tours for Jan 24 go on sale Oct 26, 2026 14:00 and sell out. Matsumoto ice festival 2027 not announced officially (2026: Jan 23–25, overnight contest Sat 16:00→Sun 5:00; one event site lists Jan 22–24, 2027). Projection mapping Dec 12, 2026–Feb 14, 2027. 21st Century Museum exhibition zones close on Mondays. Heavy snow can delay the buses.

experience.hook: Six days, six snow scenes, from a black castle to crab in Kanazawa.
moments: Watch ice carvers work all night under Matsumoto Castle, then see the finished sculptures at sunrise.
Stand on the Shiroyama deck above Shirakawa-go as the thatched roofs light up gold in deep snow.
Ride the double-decker Shinhotaka gondola to 2,156 m and look at the white Northern Alps from the roof deck.
Walk into Kenrokuen at 6:00 for free, when the rope 'snow umbrellas' over the pines are empty of crowds.
Eat male snow crab (kano-gani) at Omicho, then take the Thunderbird to Kyoto.
experience.tip: Put an alarm for Oct 26, 2026, 14:00 JST: Jan 24 light-up bus seats open then and go fast.

title: Nozawa ski, then Hokuriku west
titleJa: 野沢温泉スキー・白川郷・金沢・永平寺→京都
summary: D5 (Sat Jan 23) Hakutaka Tokyo→Iiyama (1 h 51, ¥8,360 unreserved), Nozawa Onsen Liner bus (25 min, ¥600), ski the afternoon, soak in the free wooden soto-yu baths · D6 (Sun Jan 24) ski until 11:00, Iiyama→Kanazawa (1 h 18, ¥6,730), 14:30 Hokutetsu light-up tour to Shirakawa-go with deck ticket (back 21:50, ¥18,500) · D7 (Mon) Kenrokuen early free entry, Omicho crab, Higashi Chaya (museum closed Mondays) · D8 (Tue) 21st Century Museum at 10:00, Tsurugi to Fukui (35 min), Eiheiji temple in snow, evening Thunderbird Fukui→Kyoto (1 h 27, ¥5,930) · D9–D10 Kyoto/Osaka, fly to Hokkaido from Itami/KIX.
why: Pegasis gets a real ski day on big Nozawa slopes (Aoki can take a lesson), and the Shinkansen line makes it a straight line west with no bus transfers except the light-up tour.
cost: Transport approx ¥22,000 pp (8,360 + 600 + 6,730 + 3,210 + 5,930 incl. local) + Nozawa 1-day lift ¥7,800 (4-hour ¥6,700) + light-up tour ¥18,500 + Eiheiji ¥700
winterNote: New route days 5–10. Nozawa 2026–27 regular season Dec 19, 2026–Mar 28, 2027. Light-up tour seats for Jan 24 open Oct 26, 2026 14:00 (Hokutetsu, web or phone). Fukui Dinosaur Museum is NOT possible here: closed Jan 25–28, 2027 for maintenance (plus 2nd/4th Wednesdays).

experience.hook: Ski a snow-village mountain, then see Shirakawa-go lit up the same night.
moments: Ski Nozawa's long runs from the Nagasaka gondola while the beginner takes a morning ski-school lesson.
Soak in Oyu, the wooden public bath in the village centre, and drop a coin in the donation box.
Ride the evening bus from Kanazawa and watch Shirakawa-go's thatched roofs glow from the viewpoint deck.
Walk Eiheiji's covered wooden corridors in snow while monks in black robes move between halls.
Arrive in Kyoto on the Thunderbird in about 90 minutes from Fukui.
experience.tip: Send big bags from Tokyo to your Kanazawa hotel by takkyubin, so you carry only ski clothes to Nozawa.

title: Shirakawa-go light-up: 2027 ticket guide
titleJa: 白川郷ライトアップ2027 予約方法
summary: Updated, more complete version of the existing Shirakawa-go light-up idea: all 2027 dates and every way in. Dates are Jan 11, 17, 24 and 31, 2027, 17:30–19:30; from 15:30 a gate closes the village to anyone without a ticket.
why: Jan 24 falls on new route day 6, and choosing the right tour (with or without the viewpoint deck) decides whether you get the famous photo.
cost: Takayama Nohi tours: A ¥13,000 (folk museum + zenzai), B ¥16,000 (deck ticket), C ¥14,000 (Shirakawa-go no Yu onsen); Kanazawa Hokutetsu tour ¥18,500 (deck ticket); parking for own car ¥6,000 (1–5 people, first sale) / ¥7,000 (second sale), no deck
winterNote: New route day 6 (Sun Jan 24, 2027). Sale dates for route-bus tours (Nohi, Kaetsuno, Toyama Chitetsu, Hokutetsu, Iruka), 14:00 JST: Jan 11 → Oct 13; Jan 17 → Oct 19; Jan 24 → Oct 26; Jan 31 → Nov 2, 2026. Inn-with-deck lottery Oct 1–31, 2026 (results Nov 10). Parking sale 1 opened Sep 10, 2026; sale 2 Dec 1, 2026 13:00; parking has no deck access, enter 15:00, leave by 20:00. Travel-agency tours published Dec 2, 2026. Regular route buses must arrive before 15:20. Cancelled only if heavy snow stops the event.

places.ja: 高山濃飛バスセンター

experience.hook: Four nights a year, and only ticket holders get past the gate.
moments: Get off the tour bus in the blue dusk while snow squeaks under your boots.
Walk the main street as the windows of old farmhouses light up one by one.
Climb to the Shiroyama deck at 17:30 and see the whole valley of lit thatched roofs below.
Warm your hands on a hot drink before the bus leaves at the set time.
experience.tip: Only tours marked 'deck ticket' (Nohi Course B, Hokutetsu) let you up to the viewpoint. Book one at exactly 14:00 JST on sale day.

title: Matsumoto ice sculptures and castle show
titleJa: 国宝松本城氷彫フェスティバル・プロジェクションマッピング
summary: On the last weekend of January, ice carvers compete all night in Matsumoto Castle Park, and the finished sculptures stand in front of the castle at dawn. In the evening a free projection-mapping show plays on the castle tower.
why: A new angle on Matsumoto (the castle itself is already in the Alps idea): it lines up with new route day 5 (Sat Jan 23) and gives a free night show plus a sunrise photo.
cost: Festival and projection mapping free; castle keep ¥1,300 (not re-checked for 2027)
winterNote: New route days 5–6. 2027 festival dates not officially announced; 2026 was Fri Jan 23–Sun Jan 25 with the championship carving Sat 16:00→Sun 5:00 and display Sun 5:00–about 14:00. An event listing site gives Jan 22–24, 2027. Projection mapping 2026–27: Dec 12, 2026–Feb 14, 2027, 18:00–22:00 (confirmed by Matsumoto tourism). Castle closed Dec 29–31 only.

experience.hook: Ice carvers work all night under a black castle; you see the result at dawn.
moments: Watch the projection show play on the castle tower in a loop after 18:00.
Stand by the moat at night and hear chainsaws and chisels as carvers shape big ice blocks.
Walk back at sunrise to see the finished sculptures lit pink against the snowy Alps.
Warm up with soba and hot sake on Nawate street, the frog-themed shopping lane.
experience.tip: Stay in a hotel near the castle, not the station, so the dawn walk to the sculptures is only a few minutes.

title: Takayama morning market and sake shops
titleJa: 宮川朝市・陣屋前朝市・古い町並の造り酒屋
summary: Two morning markets (Miyagawa along the river, Jinya-mae in front of the old government office) sell pickles, miso and hot snacks; in winter they open later. Then walk the Sanmachi lanes where six old sake breweries sell new-season sake with tastings.
why: New angle vs the Hida anime idea: a slow, tasty morning in the snow town, with new-season sake that only appears in winter.
cost: Market snacks ¥300–800; sake tasting about ¥500–1,000 (varies by shop, not checked for 2027)
winterNote: New route day 7. Miyagawa market daily 8:00–12:00 in Dec–Mar (7:00 other months). Jinya-mae market Jan–Mar 7:00–12:00 (source varies: 7:00 or 8:00). The old winter 'sake brewery open week' rotation (6 breweries, one per week, Jan–Mar) was last confirmed in 2019; 2027 not announced. The summer sake event (Nonbe Matsuri) is not in January.

experience.hook: A riverside market in snow, then new sake under green cedar balls.
moments: Walk the Miyagawa riverside stalls and try hot mitarashi dango grilled with soy.
Buy red-turnip pickles and hoba miso from grandmothers at the Jinya-mae stalls.
Look for the fresh green cedar ball (sugidama) over brewery doors: it means new sake is ready.
Taste Hida sake side by side at a Kami-Sannomachi brewery counter.
Eat Hida beef nigiri on a rice cracker at a Sanmachi street stand.
experience.tip: Go at 9:00 in winter; stalls open at 8:00 but set up slowly in the cold.

title: Hida Folk Village snow light-up
titleJa: 飛騨の里 冬のライトアップ
summary: Hida no Sato, an open-air museum of thatched gassho farmhouses on a pond in Takayama, lights them up every evening in winter. It is a cheap, no-booking backup if Shirakawa-go light-up tickets are gone.
why: The same snow-roof farmhouse scene, 10 minutes from Takayama, for ¥300 and without a lottery.
cost: ¥300 (light-up hours)
winterNote: New route days 6–7. 2027 winter light-up: Jan 9 (Sat)–Feb 28, 2027, every day, 17:30–20:30 (announced by Hida no Sato). Free amazake and shiitake tea were served in 2026.

experience.hook: Thatched farmhouses glowing on a frozen pond, no ticket lottery needed.
moments: Walk the snow path around the pond as lamps light the steep thatched roofs.
Take the reflection photo of the houses across the pond before it gets fully dark.
Drink the free hot amazake by the entrance (served in past years).
Take a taxi back to Takayama for a Hida beef dinner.
experience.tip: Arrive at 17:30 for the blue-hour sky; by 18:30 the photos are just black and gold.

title: Shinhotaka Ropeway and Okuhida onsen
titleJa: 新穂高ロープウェイ・奥飛騨温泉郷（平湯・福地）
summary: Ride Japan's only double-decker ropeway to Nishi-Hotaka-guchi (2,156 m) for a deck view of the snowy Northern Alps. On the way back, soak in the big open-air baths of Hirayu no Mori and see an ice-wall light-up in Fukuchi.
why: It is the highest snow view on this route and pairs it with onsen, which both travellers want.
duration: 1 day from Takayama (or 1 night in Okuhida)
cost: 'Okuhida Marugoto Value Kippu' 2-day from Takayama ¥7,700 (bus Takayama–Shinhotaka + ropeway round trip; ropeway alone ¥3,800); Hirayu no Mori day bath ¥700
winterNote: New route day 7. Ropeway runs all year; winter timetable Dec 1–Mar 31: first car 9:00, last down about 16:15; stops in bad weather. Nabedaira car park closed in snow season. Shinhotaka no Yu river bath is closed Oct 31–late April. Fukuchi 'Aodaru' ice light-up and Shin-Hirayu 'Taruma Kaneko-ori' ice light-up ran late Dec–Feb/Mar in 2025–26 (2027 not announced). Hirayu ice falls festival is Feb 15–25 and Nakao kamakura Feb 1–10 (after this stretch). Takayama→ropeway about 1 h 40 by bus.

experience.hook: A two-storey gondola lifts you to 2,156 m of snow and Alps.
moments: Stand at the front window of the double-decker gondola as the forest turns white below.
Walk onto the roof deck at Nishi-Hotaka-guchi and see Yarigatake's sharp peak in the cold air.
Eat the 'itadaki' churros shaped like the kanji for summit at the top café.
Soak in one of Hirayu no Mori's many outdoor baths with snow piled on the rocks.
See Fukuchi's lit blue-white ice walls after dark if you stay the night.
experience.tip: Go up on the first car at 9:00; clouds often build after noon and hide the peaks.

title: Kanazawa in snow: garden, crab, art
titleJa: 兼六園の雪吊り・近江町市場・ひがし茶屋街・21世紀美術館
summary: Enter Kenrokuen free before 7:45 to see the rope 'yukitsuri' snow umbrellas, eat crab at Omicho Market, walk the Higashi Chaya teahouse street and see the 21st Century Museum pool. New details for late January are in the notes.
why: Kanazawa is the natural overnight between Shirakawa-go and Kyoto, and this day gives food, gardens and art with smart timing.
cost: Kenrokuen ¥320 (free 6:00–7:45); crab: set meals and whole male crabs vary widely, often ¥5,000+ (not checked); 21st Century Museum exhibition about ¥450–1,200 (varies); Higashi Chaya street free
winterNote: New route days 8–9. Kenrokuen Oct 16–end Feb 8:00–17:00; free early entry Nov–Feb 6:00–7:45 (last entry 7:30) via Renchimon or Zuishinzaka gates only. Garden winter light-up 2027 is Feb 6–10, 13, 20, 27 (after this trip). Omicho 9:00–17:00 (Sun/holidays 9:00–16:00), no eating while walking. Local female kobako crab is only sold until December; in late Jan local crab is the male kano-gani (season Nov 6–Mar 20). 21st Century Museum: exhibition zones closed Mondays (Jan 25, 2027 is a Monday); Swimming Pool underground needs a same-day time slot from 9:00 plus an exhibition ticket.

experience.hook: Snow ropes over 300-year-old pines, then crab for breakfast.
moments: Walk into Kenrokuen at 6:30 for free and see the Karasaki pine's cone of ropes over the frozen pond.
Eat a kaisen-don or boiled kano-gani crab at an Omicho counter while the fish sellers shout prices.
Walk Higashi Chaya's wooden teahouse lane and try gold-leaf soft serve.
Look up through the water of Leandro Erlich's Swimming Pool, then stand under it.
experience.tip: Book the Swimming Pool slot on the museum site at 9:00 the same morning; afternoon slots go first on weekends.

title: Fukui: Eiheiji in snow, dinosaurs
titleJa: 大本山永平寺・福井県立恐竜博物館・東尋坊
summary: Stop in Fukui between Kanazawa and Kyoto: Eiheiji is a working Zen training temple in cedar forest, very quiet in snow. The Fukui Prefectural Dinosaur Museum is one of the world's big dinosaur museums, but it is closed on most of our dates.
why: Fukui is directly on the Kanazawa→Kyoto line (Tsurugi stops there), so it costs almost no extra travel time.
cost: Eiheiji ¥700; Eiheiji Liner bus from Fukui Station about 30 min; Dinosaur Museum ¥1,000 (timed reservation)
winterNote: New route days 8–9. Eiheiji open 8:30–16:30 (enter by 16:00). Dinosaur Museum: closed 2nd/4th Wednesdays (Jan 13 and 27, 2027) AND planned maintenance closure Jan 25–28, 2027, so on this stretch it only works on Jan 23–24 or from Jan 29. Tojinbo cliffs are open-air and free; winter waves are strong, keep back from the edge.

experience.hook: A silent Zen temple in snowy cedars, right on your way to Kyoto.
moments: Take off your shoes and walk Eiheiji's long wooden stair corridors between snow-covered halls.
Look up at the 230 painted ceiling panels of the Sanshokaku hall.
Eat Echizen oroshi soba with grated radish near the temple gate.
If you have a free day after Jan 28, stand under the full T. rex skeletons at the Dinosaur Museum.
experience.tip: Leave big bags in Fukui Station lockers; the temple has many steep stairs.

title: Toyama stop: glass art and shrimp
titleJa: 富山市ガラス美術館・白えび亭
summary: Toyama is the Shinkansen gateway to Takayama (Hida express, 1 h 31). In winter the mountain sights are closed, so the stop is the Kengo Kuma-designed Glass Art Museum and a white shrimp bowl at the station.
why: If you come from Tokyo by Shinkansen instead of via Matsumoto, this makes the change of trains into a good 2-hour stop.
cost: Glass museum collection ¥200; shiro-ebi tendon about ¥1,500–2,000 (not checked)
winterNote: New route day 6 (if you go Tokyo→Toyama→Takayama). Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route is CLOSED in winter (closed from Dec 1, reopens mid-April; 2026 opened Apr 15). Kurobe Gorge trolley train is CLOSED (runs about Apr–Nov 30). Glass museum 9:30–18:00, closed 1st and 3rd Wednesdays (Jan 6 and 20, 2027). White shrimp fishing is Apr–Nov, so in January you eat frozen stock. Himi 'kan-buri' winter yellowtail brand season often ends in mid/late January.

experience.hook: A wooden library-museum full of glass, then a bowl of tiny sweet shrimp.
moments: Walk up through the cedar-slat atrium of the TOYAMA Kirari building.
See Dale Chihuly's glass garden room on the 6th floor.
Eat a shiro-ebi tendon, a pile of small crisp white shrimp, at Shiroebi-tei in the station.
Catch the Hida express to Takayama along the snowy Jinzu river gorge.
experience.tip: Sit on the right side of the Hida train toward Takayama for river views.

title: Nozawa Onsen ski stop en route
titleJa: 野沢温泉スキー場・外湯めぐり
summary: Nozawa Onsen is a ski village 25 minutes by bus from Iiyama Station, which is on the Hokuriku Shinkansen between Tokyo and Kanazawa. Ski a day, then walk the snowy lanes between 13 free public baths.
why: New angle vs the Hakuba idea: it sits on the westward Shinkansen line, so skiing does not cost an extra travel day, and the free baths suit both.
cost: Lift 1 day ¥7,800, 4 h ¥6,700, 2 days ¥14,500 (2026–27 regular); Nozawa Onsen Liner ¥600 each way; Tokyo→Iiyama ¥8,360 unreserved; soto-yu baths free (donation)
winterNote: New route days 5–6. Regular season prices Dec 19, 2026–Mar 28, 2027. Dosojin fire festival is Jan 15 (before arrival). Hakuba (existing idea) needs a 1 h+ bus from Nagano instead, so Nozawa is the easier stop on this route. Iiyama→Kanazawa 1 h 18 (¥6,730).

experience.hook: A ski resort where the public baths are free and the village steams.
moments: Ride the Nagasaka gondola and ski the Skyline course with views to the Sea of Japan side mountains.
Let the beginner practise on the wide Uenotaira area slopes.
Walk the snowy lanes at night between wooden bathhouses like Oyu and Kuma no Tearaiyu.
Watch locals boil eggs and vegetables in the 90°C Ogama spring.
experience.tip: The soto-yu water is very hot; add cold water slowly and bring your own small towel.

title: Kanazawa to Kyoto/Osaka: train facts
titleJa: 金沢→京都・大阪（北陸新幹線つるぎ＋サンダーバード）
summary: Since 2024 you take the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Tsuruga and change on the same platform area to the Thunderbird. Kanazawa→Kyoto is about 2 h 04 (¥7,720) and →Osaka about 2 h 31 (¥9,410), reserved seats.
why: This is the key link from the Alps side to the Osaka flight, and there are cheaper ways if you plan ahead.
cost: Reserved: Kyoto ¥7,720, Osaka ¥9,410, Kansai Airport ¥11,080 (3 h 43). Unreserved Shinkansen + local Special Rapid: Osaka ¥7,480, 3 h 23. All-local: ¥5,040, about 5 h. JR-West 'HOKURIKU One-way Ticket' for foreign tourists: Kanazawa→Osaka ¥8,000, →Kyoto ¥6,500 (buy from overseas agency, not in Japan).
winterNote: New route days 9–10. Times/fares from Yahoo Transit for a normal weekday in 2026. Snow can delay the Thunderbird around Lake Biwa. Fukui→Kyoto 1 h 27 (¥5,930) if you stop in Fukui. For Itami airport, bus from Osaka/Shin-Osaka about 25–30 min.

experience.hook: Two trains, one easy change, snow coast to Kyoto in two hours.
moments: Board the Tsurugi Shinkansen at Kanazawa with a bento from the station.
Change at Tsuruga: the Thunderbird leaves from the platforms downstairs, about 10–15 minutes later.
Watch Lake Biwa pass on the left before Kyoto.
experience.tip: Buy one ticket Kanazawa→Kyoto/Osaka covering both trains; it gives you both seat reservations in one go.

title: Takayama to Nagoya or Osaka
titleJa: 高山→名古屋・大阪（特急ひだ・高速バス）
summary: From Takayama you can go straight south to Osaka without Kanazawa: one direct Hida train a day, or Hida to Nagoya plus Shinkansen, or a highway bus. Matsumoto→Takayama is by reserved bus only.
why: If you skip Kanazawa, this is the fastest way from the snow town to the Osaka flight, with a Toyota Museum stop possible in Nagoya.
cost: Direct Hida 36: Takayama 15:34→Osaka 19:50, ¥7,920 unreserved. Hida + Nozomi via Nagoya: 3 h 47, ¥11,110. Hida to Nagoya: 2 h 28, ¥5,610. Nohi bus to Nagoya ¥3,600 (web ¥3,300, about 2 h 35–2 h 45). Nohi/Kintetsu bus to Kyoto ¥6,500 / Osaka ¥7,000 (5 h 40; dep. 8:00, 10:10, 13:40). Matsumoto→Takayama bus ¥4,400 (2 h 20–2 h 50).
winterNote: New route days 8–9. Timetables checked Sep 2026 for the current timetable; January can differ. Buses need a reservation (1 month ahead). Snow can slow the Hida line and the Gujo route.

places.ja: 高山駅・高山濃飛バスセンター

experience.hook: One seat from the snowy Alps town to Osaka, along a river gorge.
moments: Board the new HC85 Hida train at Takayama with Hida beef bento.
Watch the Hida river gorge and Gero onsen town pass in the snow.
Stay seated through Kyoto and step off at Osaka in the evening.
experience.tip: The direct Hida to Osaka runs once a day in the afternoon; reserve it, the Osaka cars are few.

title: Alps/Hokuriku rail passes: buy or skip
titleJa: 高山・北陸エリア周遊きっぷ／北陸アーチパス等の比較
summary: We checked every pass for this area in 2026. Only the Takayama-Hokuriku pass and the Kansai-Hokuriku pass can be used in January, and for the plans above single tickets are about the same or cheaper.
why: Passes cost ¥19,000–35,000, so a wrong pick wastes money; this shows which one fits which route.
cost: Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass ¥19,800 / 5 days; Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto ¥24,500 / 5 days (not usable in winter); Hokuriku Arch Pass ¥35,000 / 7 days; Kansai-Hokuriku Area Pass ¥19,000 / 7 days; Hokuriku Area Pass ¥7,000 / 4 days
winterNote: New route days 5–10. Takayama-Hokuriku: JR Nagoya–Takayama–Toyama, Toyama–Tsuruga Shinkansen, Tsuruga–Kyoto–Osaka, Osaka–KIX, plus Nohi/Hokutetsu/Toyama Chitetsu buses Takayama–Shirakawa-go–Kanazawa/Toyama (some need reservations); no Matsumoto, no light-up tours. Plan A legs it covers (Takayama→Kanazawa ¥4,200 + Kanazawa→Osaka ¥9,410) = ¥13,610, less than ¥19,800. Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto: usage period Apr 15–Nov 10, 2026 only. Hokuriku Arch: Narita/Haneda–Tokyo–Kanazawa–Osaka–KIX; Tokyo→Kanazawa ¥14,600 + Kanazawa→Osaka ¥9,410 = ¥24,010, so it only pays with extra trips (N'EX, Haruka, Toyama/Fukui side trips). Kansai-Hokuriku: Joetsu-Myoko–Tsuruga Shinkansen + Kansai; good only if you also stay several Kansai days on JR. All need a foreign passport and 'Temporary Visitor' entry.

experience.hook: Most passes here lose money on this route; pick single tickets or one-way deals.
moments: Add up your real legs first: Tokyo→Kanazawa ¥14,600, Kanazawa→Osaka ¥9,410.
Use the Takayama-Hokuriku pass only if you add Toyama, Fukui or a Kansai Airport ride within 5 days.
Buy the ¥8,000 Hokuriku One-way Ticket (Kanazawa→Osaka) from an overseas agency before you fly.
experience.tip: The Alpine-Takayama-Matsumoto pass looks perfect on maps, but it is not valid after Nov 10, 2026.

title: Fushimi Inari dawn, Kinkakuji snow
titleJa: 伏見稲荷大社（早朝）・金閣寺（雪景色）
summary: Walk the Fushimi Inari torii tunnels at 7:00, before the crowds, then go to Kinkakuji for its 9:00 opening. If snow fell in the night, the gold temple has a white roof, which happens only 1-3 mornings a winter.
why: Gives the two most famous Kyoto photos without the crowds, and a real chance of the rare snowy gold temple.
cost: Fushimi Inari free; Kinkakuji ¥500; trains/bus approx ¥600
winterNote: New route day 8 (or any Kyoto morning). Fushimi Inari is open 24 h, free. Kinkakuji opens 9:00-17:00. Settled snow at Kinkakuji is about 1-3 days a year (first snow of winter 2025-26 was Jan 3, 2026); check the forecast the night before. Arashiyama Hanatouro ended in 2021; its bamboo light-up 'Tsukitouro' was on Jan 10-11 in 2026, so not in your dates.

experience.hook: Empty orange torii at dawn, then maybe a gold temple under snow.
moments: Walk the Senbon Torii tunnel at 7:00 with only the sound of your boots and crows.
Climb 30 minutes to the Yotsutsuji crossing and look down over south Kyoto in cold clear air.
Stand at the Kinkakuji pond edge at 9:00 opening and find the gold pavilion in its mirror.
Eat a hot yudofu or kitsune udon lunch near the station to warm your hands.
experience.tip: Look at the Kyoto snow forecast at night. With snow, skip Inari and be at the Kinkakuji gate before 9:00.

title: Kyoto winter secret temple openings
titleJa: 第61回 京の冬の旅 非公開文化財特別公開
summary: Every winter Kyoto City opens temple rooms, paintings and gardens that are closed the rest of the year. Pick 1-3 sites (about ¥800 each); after 3 stamps you get free tea and a sweet.
why: Quiet, heated-by-nobody old rooms with few foreign visitors: a real 'insider' Kyoto moment on a cold day.
cost: approx ¥800 per site (2026 price)
winterNote: New route day 8-9. The 61st edition in Jan-Mar 2027 is sold by tour companies, but the 2027 site list is not announced (usually out in November). 2026 (60th) ran Jan 9 - Mar 18, 2026, ¥800 per site. Some sites have short early-morning special slots.
photoQuery: Kyoto temple interior winter fusuma painting

experience.hook: Step into Kyoto rooms that open only in winter.
moments: Take off your shoes and walk in socks on ice-cold wooden floors past gold screen paintings.
Listen to the volunteer guide explain each room (Japanese; take photos where allowed).
Collect 3 stamps on the card and swap it for hot matcha and a Kyoto sweet.
Warm up afterwards in a kissaten with a thick toast and coffee.
experience.tip: Wear thick socks: the halls have no heating. Check the 2027 list in November and pick sites near your route.

title: Kurama to Kibune snowy hike
titleJa: 鞍馬寺・貴船神社（雪景色）
summary: Take the small Eizan train north of Kyoto to Kurama, climb through Kurama-dera temple and over the hill to Kibune (about 1.5 h). Kifune Shrine's red lantern steps look best with snow; on snowy weekends the shrine lights them up at night.
why: A cold mountain valley 30 minutes from Kyoto with a good chance of snow, a forest walk, and a famous lantern stair photo.
cost: Eizan train approx ¥470 each way; Kurama-dera approx ¥500; Kifune shrine free
winterNote: Kibune gets snow more often than Kyoto city. Kifune snow-day light-up in 2026: Jan 17 - Feb 28, Saturdays and Sundays only, sunset to 20:30, only when snow lies (cancelled on Jan 24, 2026 for no snow). 2027 not announced. New route: weekend days 5-6 (Jan 23-24) or 12-13 if you are in Kansai then; on weekdays you still get the snow walk but no light-up. Kurama cable car was stopped for repair and came back on Sep 1, 2026. The hill path is icy: wear shoes with grip.

experience.hook: Red lanterns, white steps: Kyoto's snow valley is 30 minutes away.
moments: Ride the one-car Eizan train as the houses turn into cedar forest.
Climb Kurama-dera's stone steps to the main hall and see the Kyoto hills under snow.
Walk down the root-covered forest path into Kibune, the river loud under the ice.
Stand at the foot of Kifune Shrine's lantern stairs, red posts against snow.
Finish with a hot soak at Kurama Onsen's outdoor bath if you have time.
experience.tip: Follow @kifunejinja on X: it posts by noon if the snow light-up is on that evening.

title: Ohara village temples in snow
titleJa: 大原 三千院・寂光院
summary: Take the bus one hour north to Ohara, a farm valley that is colder and snowier than Kyoto. See the moss garden and small smiling jizo statues of Sanzen-in, then walk the quiet lanes to Jakko-in.
why: A slow, calm day after busy Tokyo: snowy moss garden, hot tea, pickles, and almost no crowds in winter.
cost: Sanzen-in ¥700; Kyoto Bus approx ¥600 each way
winterNote: New route day 8-9. Sanzen-in is open every day; Dec-Feb hours 9:00-16:30. Ohara often has snow when Kyoto city has none, but not always.

experience.hook: Moss, snow and tiny smiling stone monks in a mountain valley.
moments: Sit on the tatami of Sanzen-in's hall and look out at the Yusei-en garden.
Find the small warabe jizo statues peeking out of the moss (or the snow).
Taste shiba-zuke pickles free in the shops along the approach path.
Walk 20 minutes past rice fields to quiet Jakko-in.
experience.tip: Go early and take Kyoto Bus 17 from Kyoto Station; the last good buses back leave before 17:00.

title: Nara deer and hill-burning festival
titleJa: 若草山焼き2027・奈良公園・東大寺
summary: On Sat Jan 23, 2027 Nara sets a whole grass hill on fire after 600 fireworks. Spend the afternoon with the deer and the giant Buddha at Todaiji, then watch the hill burn from Nara Park at 18:30.
why: Fireworks in January plus a mountain on fire is a once-a-year scene, and it fits right after the Tokyo days.
cost: Festival free; Todaiji Great Buddha Hall ¥800; deer crackers ¥200; train Kyoto-Nara approx ¥760
winterNote: New route day 5 (Sat Jan 23, 2027). Date is set by the Nara festival committee (Nara Prefecture notice, Sep 2026): 17:40 Nogami Shrine rite, 18:15 fireworks, 18:30 fire. Cancelled in bad weather, with no second date. To be there you must leave Tokyo by the morning of D5.

experience.hook: 600 fireworks, then a whole hill in Nara goes up in flames.
moments: Bow to a deer and watch it bow back before you give it a cracker.
Stand below the 15 m bronze Great Buddha inside Todaiji's huge wooden hall.
Eat hot kakinoha sushi or kamameshi as the sky gets dark.
Watch fireworks over Wakakusa-yama at 18:15, then see the flames climb the hill at 18:30.
experience.tip: Get a place in Nara Park near Todaiji or by Sarusawa Pond by 17:30; the base of the hill is packed.

title: Kobe beef, sake cellars, Kitano
titleJa: 神戸牛ランチ・灘五郷酒蔵・北野異人館
summary: Eat a real Kobe beef teppanyaki lunch in Sannomiya, walk up to the old Western houses of Kitano, then taste free sake at the Nada brewery museums (Hakutsuru, Kikumasamune).
why: Kobe beef is a bucket-list meal, and the free sake museums make the rest of the day cheap.
cost: Real Kobe beef lunch approx ¥6,000-15,000 (cheaper 'wagyu' lunches from ¥1,500 are not Kobe beef); sake museums free; Hanshin train approx ¥200
winterNote: New route day 10-11. All indoor or city streets. Sake museums: Kikumasamune 9:30-16:30, free, closed at New Year only; January is the brewing season, the cellars smell of rice.

experience.hook: Kobe beef on a hot iron plate, then free sake in the cellar.
moments: Watch the chef sear Kobe beef on the teppan and slice it in front of you.
Walk the steep Kitano lanes past the Weathercock House and 1900s Western homes.
See wooden sake tanks and old tools in the Hakutsuru museum, then taste the new-season sake.
Try a cup of Kikumasamune's dry 'karakuchi' sake in the free tasting corner.
experience.tip: Check the 'Kobe Beef' certificate (nose print) in the shop. Lunch sets cost about half of the same dinner.

title: Kobe night view and Luminarie
titleJa: 摩耶山 掬星台・神戸ルミナリエ2027
summary: Ride the Maya cable car and ropeway to Kikuseidai for the 'ten-million-dollar' night view of Kobe and Osaka Bay. On Jan 29 - Feb 7, 2027 the Kobe Luminarie light arches also stand in the city below.
why: Japan's top-3 night view plus the opening night of a famous light festival, both in one Friday evening.
cost: Maya cable + ropeway round trip ¥1,560; Luminarie free, paid Meriken Park zone ¥500-750 advance / ¥1,000-1,500 on the day
winterNote: New route day 11 (Fri Jan 29, 2027 = Luminarie first night). Luminarie 2027 (32nd): Jan 29 - Feb 7, dusk to 21:30. Maya Viewline winter hours (Nov 1 - Mar 19): CLOSED Tuesdays; Mon/Wed/Thu last ride up 16:40 (no night view); Fri/Sat/Sun/holidays last up 19:20. So night view only Fri-Sun. Stops in strong wind.
photoQuery: Kikuseidai Mount Maya night view Kobe

experience.hook: Kobe's harbour lights spread below you like spilled gold.
moments: Ride the old cable car, then the ropeway, up 700 m in the last light.
Stand at Kikuseidai at 18:00 and trace the city from Akashi Bridge to Osaka.
Ride down and walk into the glowing Luminarie arches downtown.
Eat hot steamed pork buns in Nankinmachi Chinatown after.
experience.tip: Go on Friday: take the 18:20 or 18:40 cable car up. Last car down leaves the top at 19:50.

title: Himeji Castle, the white heron
titleJa: 姫路城
summary: Japan's best original castle, all white, 6 floors of wood inside. Climb steep wooden stairs to the top, then walk the Kokoen garden next door.
why: The most famous castle in Japan, 45 minutes from Kyoto by Shinkansen and easy to join with Kobe or Kinosaki.
cost: ¥2,500 for visitors who do not live in Himeji (from Mar 1, 2026; was ¥1,000); Shinkansen Kyoto-Himeji approx ¥5,000
winterNote: New route day 9-10. Open 9:00-17:00, last entry 16:00, closed only Dec 29-30. The yearly 'winter special opening' of closed rooms starts mid-February (2025: Feb 15 - Mar 2), so not in your dates. Snow here is rare.

experience.hook: Climb inside a 400-year-old wooden castle that never burned.
moments: Walk straight from the station up Otemae street with the white keep growing ahead.
Climb six floors of steep, polished wooden stairs in socks, holding the rope rail.
Look out from the top floor window over the grey roofs to the sea.
Eat Himeji oden with ginger soy sauce near the station.
experience.tip: Arrive at 9:00. Coin lockers at Himeji Station take big suitcases; the castle has none.

title: Arima gold and silver springs
titleJa: 有馬温泉 金の湯・銀の湯
summary: Arima, 30 minutes from Kobe, has two kinds of water: rusty-red 'gold' salt water and clear 'silver' water. Do both public baths on a 2-bath ticket, walk the steep lanes, and ride the Rokko-Arima ropeway.
why: One of Japan's oldest onsen and an easy half day from Kobe, with a real 'red water' you will not find elsewhere.
cost: Kin no yu ¥800 (weekdays ¥650); 2-bath ticket ¥1,200; bus/train from Sannomiya approx ¥700-1,000 each way
winterNote: New route day 10-11. Kin no yu: 8:00-22:00, closed 2nd and 4th Tuesday of the month, so CLOSED on Tue Jan 26, 2027 (D8). It reopened Mar 17, 2026 after works. Rokko-Arima ropeway runs in winter; check for wind.

experience.hook: Soak in rust-red iron water that stains your towel orange.
moments: Put your feet in the free gold-water footbath outside Kin no yu.
Sink into Kin no yu's brown, salty 'gold' water.
Walk up the lanes to Gin no yu for a clear 'silver' soak.
Eat a warm tansan senbei (soda cracker) baked on the street.
Ride the Rokko-Arima ropeway over snowy slopes back toward Kobe.
experience.tip: Go on a weekday morning: Kin no yu is ¥650 and quiet. Bring an old towel, the iron water stains.

title: Kinosaki bath-hopping in crab season
titleJa: 城崎温泉 外湯めぐり・松葉ガニ
summary: Stay one night in Kinosaki, a willow-lined canal town on the Sea of Japan side. Walk in yukata and wooden geta between 6 public baths with a free pass from your ryokan, and eat Matsuba snow crab.
why: The classic Japanese onsen town night, often with snow, plus winter crab: a big contrast to cities.
cost: Ltd exp Kyoto-Kinosaki approx ¥5,200-5,400 one way (2 h 20 min); bath day pass 'Yumepa' ¥1,500 (single ¥800), free for most ryokan guests; ryokan with crab dinner approx ¥25,000-45,000 pp (varies); ryokan crab lunch without stay from ¥10,450
winterNote: New route day 9-10. Crab season Nov 6 to March. Only 6 of 7 baths are open: Satono-yu closed since Apr 2024 and will reopen around Mar 2030. Kou-no-yu was closed May-Oct 2026 and should be open again. Each bath closes one weekday (e.g. Ichi-no-yu Wednesday, Gosho-no-yu Thursday); Mandara-yu and Yanagi-yu open at 15:00. Snow is common in January.

experience.hook: Yukata, wooden sandals and snow: hop between six hot baths all night.
moments: Change into the ryokan yukata and clack along the canal in geta under snowy willows.
Soak in Gosho-no-yu's outdoor bath beside a waterfall wall.
Try Ichi-no-yu's cave bath, dug into the rock.
Eat a crab dinner: boiled crab, grilled crab, then crab hotpot with rice porridge at the end.
Buy a hot crab bun and a local beer on the late-night walk back.
experience.tip: Your ryokan gives a free bath pass: tap it at each bath door. Go to Mandara-yu at 15:00 opening, it is empty.

title: Koyasan temple stay in snow
titleJa: 高野山 宿坊・奥之院ナイトツアー
summary: Ride the train and cable car up to Koyasan, a mountain town of 51 temples at 800 m. Sleep in a temple (shukubo), eat the monks' vegetarian dinner, walk the lantern-lit Okunoin graveyard at night, and join the fire ritual at dawn.
why: A totally different Japan: snow, cedar forest, candles and chanting, after cities and ski resorts.
cost: Shukubo with 2 meals approx ¥13,000-25,000 pp; Okunoin night tour ¥3,690 online (¥4,500 at the door; English tour approx ¥5,500-7,300); Nankai digital World Heritage ticket from Namba ¥3,980 (train + cable + local buses, round trip); Kongobuji ¥1,000
winterNote: New route day 9-10. Snow often lies in January; train and cable are the easy way (roads need chains). Cable car: closed only Dec 22-24, 2025 for cable renewal; no closure announced for Jan 2027 (checked Sep 2026). Many shukubo do NOT take guests Dec-Feb (Wakayama tourism), so book early; Eko-in runs all year. Night tour runs almost every day at 19:00-20:20, some New Year breaks.

experience.hook: Sleep in a snowy temple and walk a graveyard of 200,000 tombs by lantern light.
moments: Ride the steep cable car up through cedar forest into the snow line.
Eat shojin ryori dinner in your room: sesame tofu, tempura, pickles, all vegetables.
Walk Okunoin at 19:00 with a monk guide, moss-covered tombs lit by stone lanterns.
Sit in the dark hall at 6:30 for the morning chant and the roaring goma fire.
See the huge orange Konpon Daito pagoda standing in the snow.
experience.tip: Book a shukubo that allows the night tour; some have early bath and meal times. Bring warm socks: rooms are cold.

title: Tuna show and seaside onsen
titleJa: 黒潮市場・白浜温泉 崎の湯
summary: Watch a whole tuna cut up at Kuroshio Market (Wakayama Marina City) and eat it fresh. Or go further south to Shirahama and sit in Saki-no-yu, a rock bath right at the Pacific waves.
why: Warm, sunny coast and fresh tuna after the snow; Saki-no-yu is one of the most dramatic sea baths in Japan for ¥500.
cost: Kuroshio: show free, tuna bowls approx ¥1,500-3,000; Saki-no-yu ¥500; Osaka-Shirahama Ltd exp approx 2 h 30 min
winterNote: New route day 10, good after Koyasan (Koyasan-Hashimoto-Wakayama by train). Kuroshio tuna show: weekdays 12:30 and 15:00, weekends/holidays 11:00, 12:30, 15:00. Saki-no-yu Oct-Mar 8:00-17:00, last entry 30 min before. Adventure World's pandas went back to China in 2025.

experience.hook: Fresh tuna cut in front of you, then a hot bath at the Pacific's edge.
moments: Watch the staff cut a whole tuna into blocks while the host calls out each part.
Eat a chutoro and otoro bowl straight after the show.
Sit in Saki-no-yu's rock pool as winter waves crash a few metres away.
Try grilled seafood skewers at Toretore Market in Shirahama.
experience.tip: Buy the fresh tuna sashimi cut after the show right away: it sells out in minutes.

title: 4 Kansai days: Kyoto to Kobe
titleJa: 京都・城崎温泉・姫路・神戸 4日間
summary: D8 (Tue Jan 26) Kyoto: Fushimi Inari at 7:00, Kinkakuji 9:00 (snow chance), afternoon Kurama-Kibune snow walk · D9 (Wed) Ltd exp Kinosaki 7:32 → 9:52, 6 onsen baths, crab dinner, ryokan night · D10 (Thu) Hamakaze 7:13 → Himeji 8:54, castle at 9:00, Shinkansen to Shin-Kobe, Nada sake museums, Kobe beef dinner · D11 (Fri Jan 29) Arima Onsen gold bath in the morning, Kitano, then Maya night view (Friday hours) and Luminarie opening night; fly Itami/KIX → New Chitose on D12 morning. If you must fly on D11, skip the Friday evening. Swap: Koyasan temple night instead of Kinosaki.
why: Mixes temples, a real onsen-town night, the best castle and Kobe beef, with no car and short trains; Friday lands on Luminarie's first night.
cost: Trains approx ¥15,000-18,000 pp (Kyoto-Kinosaki ¥5,300, Kinosaki-Himeji, Himeji-Kobe, locals); entry fees approx ¥6,000 (Himeji ¥2,500); Kinosaki crab ryokan approx ¥25,000-45,000 pp; Kobe beef lunch/dinner ¥6,000-15,000
winterNote: New route day 8-11 (Jan 26-29). Tue Jan 26: Maya ropeway closed and Arima Kin no yu closed, so Kobe is on Thu/Fri. Hamakaze runs only 3 times a day (Kinosaki 7:13, 14:14, 17:17 toward Himeji); Himeji last entry 16:00, so take the 7:13. Luminarie 2027: Jan 29 - Feb 7. Kifune snow light-up is weekends only, so not on these weekdays.

experience.hook: Torii at dawn, crab in a snow town, a white castle, Kobe lights.
moments: Walk Fushimi Inari's empty torii tunnel at 7:00 on day 8.
Hop between Kinosaki's baths in yukata and eat a full crab dinner on day 9.
Climb Himeji Castle's wooden stairs right at 9:00 opening on day 10.
Eat Kobe beef from the teppan, then taste new sake in Nada.
End day 11 above Kobe at Kikuseidai, then walk under the Luminarie arches.
experience.tip: Send big bags from Kyoto to your Kobe hotel by takkyubin and travel to Kinosaki with small bags only.

title: Namba food crawl: Dotonbori to Kuromon
titleJa: 道頓堀・黒門市場・裏なんば 食べ歩き
summary: Eat your way through south Osaka in one afternoon and evening: Kuromon Market seafood skewers, takoyaki and okonomiyaki on Dotonbori under the Glico sign, then small standing bars in Ura-Namba. Everything is within 15 minutes on foot.
why: Osaka is the food city of Japan, and it is the easiest good night of the whole route: no tickets, no weather risk, and Namba is where most hotels are.
cost: about 5,000-8,000 JPY per person for many small plates and drinks
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10 (Osaka). All year. Kuromon stalls mostly open in the day and many close in late afternoon, and some close on Sundays: go before 16:00. Dotonbori and Ura-Namba are busy until late at night.

places.ja: 裏なんば 虎目横丁

experience.hook: Osaka's kitchen in one walk: market skewers, river neon, tiny standing bars.
moments: Eat a grilled scallop and a tuna skewer standing at a Kuromon Market stall in the early afternoon.
Walk to Ebisubashi bridge and take the photo with the Glico running man sign lit behind you.
Eat hot takoyaki from a Dotonbori stand, then okonomiyaki cooked on the iron plate at your table.
Find the moss-covered Fudo statue in quiet Hozenji Yokocho, a stone alley with old restaurants.
End in Ura-Namba: drink a highball and eat small plates at a standing bar for about 1,000 yen.
experience.tip: Go to Kuromon before 16:00, when stalls start to close. In Ura-Namba, pick the small bars that show prices outside.

title: Shinsekai kushikatsu and Spa World
titleJa: 新世界 串カツ・通天閣・スパワールド
summary: Eat deep-fried kushikatsu skewers in retro Shinsekai under Tsutenkaku tower, then soak for hours at Spa World, a huge hot-spring bath house next door with 'Europe' and 'Asia' bath floors and a pool. Good for a cold evening.
why: It puts the onsen interest into the Osaka stop: cheap, open late, and 2 minutes from the kushikatsu shops.
cost: Spa World 2,000 JPY weekday / 2,700 JPY weekend (with pool), 1,500 JPY without pool; +1,300 JPY after 24:00. Kushikatsu about 2,500 JPY
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. Open all year. Spa World does NOT allow tattoos (also stickers). The Europe and Asia bath floors switch between men and women each month. Kushikatsu Daruma main store: no reservations, open every day.

places.ja: 串かつだるま 新世界総本店
スパワールド 世界の大温泉

experience.hook: Fried skewers under a neon tower, then hot baths themed like different countries.
moments: Walk under Tsutenkaku tower as the neon signs of Shinsekai come on at dusk.
Eat beef, lotus root and quail-egg kushikatsu at Daruma, and dip each one only once in the shared sauce.
Soak in the themed bath floor of the month at Spa World, from Roman-style to Asian-style baths.
Sweat in the new dry sauna, then cool down and drink a cold milk in the rest area.
experience.tip: Go on a weekday: 2,000 yen instead of 2,700. Leave before 24:00 or you pay 1,300 yen more.

title: Den Den Town and Otaroad shopping
titleJa: 日本橋でんでんタウン・オタロード
summary: Osaka's Akihabara: one long street of electronics and anime shops (Sakaisuji) and the side street Otaroad full of figure, game and doujin shops. Visit Super Potato Otaroad for retro games, then Animate and Melonbooks for new goods.
why: Anime goods and retro games at Osaka prices, less crowded than Akihabara, and 10 minutes on foot from Namba.
cost: free to walk; budget for goods
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. All year. Super Potato Otaroad: weekdays 11:00-20:00, weekends 10:00-20:00, no closed days. Most shops open about 11:00; go after lunch.

places.ja: スーパーポテト オタロード店
アニメイト大阪日本橋
メロンブックス 大阪日本橋店

experience.hook: Osaka's Akihabara, smaller and cheaper, 10 minutes' walk from Dotonbori.
moments: Walk south from Namba down Otaroad, where life-size anime posters and figure shop windows line both sides.
Dig through Famicom and Super Famicom boxes at Super Potato, 'the largest retro stock in West Japan'.
Check new character goods at Animate, then doujin and art books at Melonbooks next door.
Walk back along Sakaisuji past the old electronics stores that gave Den Den Town its name.
experience.tip: Used figures and goods are often cheaper here than in Akihabara. Bring your passport: many shops give tax-free over 5,000 yen.

title: Osaka maid cafés on Otaroad
titleJa: 日本橋オタロード メイドカフェ
summary: Three real maid cafés within 300 m of each other: Maidreamin Osaka Nipponbashi Otaroad (shows, 880 JPY per hour), CCOちゃ (Cocha), called Osaka's first maid café (500 JPY entry), and e-maid, a restaurant-style café with no table charge. Pick one or two.
why: A Kansai version of the Akihabara maid café, easy to add to the Den Den Town walk, and e-maid is a calm choice if one of you finds shows too much.
cost: Maidreamin 880 JPY/h + 1 order (drinks from about 800 JPY); CCOちゃ 500 JPY entry + order; e-maid no charge, 1 order, 90 min limit
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. Open all year. Hours (2025): Maidreamin Mon-Fri 11:30-23:00, Sat-Sun 10:30-23:00, after 20:00 it becomes 'HYPER' bar mode (3,800 JPY 1 h drinks). CCOちゃ weekdays 15:00-20:00 L.O., weekends 12:00-20:00. e-maid weekdays 12:00-21:45 L.O. Check before you go.

places.ja: めいどりーみん 大阪日本橋オタロード店

experience.hook: Osaka's maid cafés: the big chain show, the oldest café, or a quiet lunch.
moments: Say the 'moe moe kyun' spell with the maids over an omelette rice with a drawn picture at Maidreamin.
Watch a short stage show, then take a cheki instant photo with the maid you pick.
Try one of 30+ drinks with funny names and a latte drawing at CCOちゃ, Osaka's first maid café.
Eat a full meal in a calm room at e-maid if you want the style without the shows.
experience.tip: Go to Maidreamin before 20:00; after that it becomes a bar with a 3,800 yen drink plan.

title: Universal Studios Japan on a weekday
titleJa: ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン
summary: A full day at USJ: Super Nintendo World with Mario Kart and the Donkey Kong Country mine-cart ride, plus Harry Potter. Late January weekdays are one of the quietest times of the year; buy an Express Pass that guarantees Nintendo area entry.
why: Super Nintendo World and Donkey Kong Country exist only here and in the US; it is the big fun day between the Tokyo and Hokkaido parts.
cost: 1-Day Studio Pass from 8,400 JPY (price changes by date); Express Pass 4 (with Donkey Kong) from 14,800 JPY, Express Pass 7 from 21,800 JPY; train from Osaka station 200 JPY
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10 (use a Tue-Thu). 25th anniversary 'Discover U!!!' runs Mar 4, 2026 - Mar 30, 2027, so it is on. The Holiday event ends Jan 17, the Nintendo 5th anniversary and the Frieren walk-through end Jan 11, 2027: they are over. 'Cool Japan' 2027 not announced; in 2026 its anime events started in spring, so likely not in late Jan. Express Pass goes on sale about 2 months before (late Nov 2026).

places.ja: ユニバーサルシティ駅
ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン

photoQuery: Super Nintendo World Universal Studios Japan

experience.hook: Ride Mario Kart and Donkey Kong's mine cart on a quiet January weekday.
moments: Walk through the green warp pipe into Super Nintendo World and hit ? blocks with a Power-Up Band.
Race in Mario Kart: Koopa's Challenge wearing AR goggles and throw shells at Bowser.
Ride Donkey Kong's Crazy Mine Cart, where the track seems to break under you.
Eat a hot butterbeer and walk Hogsmeade in the evening lights before the park closes.
experience.tip: Without Express, open the USJ app at entry and get the free Nintendo area timed ticket at once; they run out early.

title: Osaka Castle and Umeda Sky sunset
titleJa: 大阪城天守閣・梅田スカイビル空中庭園
summary: Morning or afternoon at Osaka Castle (museum tower, 8th-floor view over the moats), then go to the Umeda Sky Building's open-air roof ring at 173 m for sunset and the city lights. Both are easy by subway.
why: The two classic Osaka views in one half day, and the roof deck is an open-air walk in cold wind, a different feel from indoor Tokyo decks.
cost: Castle tower 1,200 JPY (since Apr 1, 2025); Umeda Sky observatory 2,000 JPY
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. Open all year. Umeda Sky 9:30-22:30 (last entry 22:00); the outside roof ring can close in strong wind or rain. Sunset in Osaka in late January is about 17:20.

places.ja: 梅田スカイビル 空中庭園展望台

experience.hook: A castle above stone moats, then a roof ring 173 m up at sunset.
moments: Walk over the moat bridges and past giant stone blocks to the white-and-gold castle tower.
Look out from the 8th-floor deck of the tower over the park and the business towers.
Ride the glass escalator that crosses between the two Umeda Sky towers.
Walk the open-air roof ring at sunset and watch the rivers and trains light up below.
experience.tip: Arrive at Umeda Sky 30 minutes before sunset (about 17:20). Bring gloves: the roof deck is open and windy.

title: Liberty Walk JDM Park, Sennan
titleJa: JDM PARK / LB DRIVE-IN（リバティーウォーク泉南）
summary: Liberty Walk, the famous wide-body tuning brand, opened its 'JDM PARK / LB DRIVE-IN' in Sennan in late 2025: a showroom of LB cars, goods shop and a Sanuki udon shop, 15 minutes by car from Kansai Airport. Stop here on the way to a KIX flight.
why: A real JDM place right on the way to the airport, free to visit, and no driving licence needed; Aoki can drive there if you rent a car.
cost: free entry (udon about 1,000 JPY); taxi or rental car needed
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11 (KIX flight day). Official site: 11:00-21:00, 365 days; its Instagram says 11:00-19:00, closed Thu: check. A local post (Apr 2026) says 'Sennan Saturday Night' car gathering from 20:00 every Saturday: not on the official site, so check. Udon shop 6:00-15:00. Nearest station JR Izumi-Sunagawa, about 1.7 km.

experience.hook: Liberty Walk's own drive-in: wide-body cars and udon, next to the airport.
moments: Walk around the LB wide-body cars on display, from GT-Rs to Lamborghinis with bolted-on fenders.
Look for Liberty Walk goods you cannot buy online: shirts, stickers, model cars.
Eat a bowl of Sanuki udon at Udonko inside the park before 15:00.
Drive or taxi 15 minutes to Kansai Airport for the flight north.
experience.tip: Put your big bags in a KIX coin locker or send them ahead, then come here light before an afternoon Peach flight.

title: Osaka JDM night tour, honest guide
titleJa: 大阪 JDMナイトツアー（助手席）
summary: Kansai has no fixed 'Daikoku' meet: the famous Nanagan pier closed in 2017, and NEXCO closes Higashi-Osaka PA and Yao PA with police when crowds get dangerous. The reliable way is a guided passenger tour (e.g. 'JDM Car Meet Up Tour in Osaka', from about US$137) or MR.HIRO's guided drive if Aoki has 3+ years of manual driving.
why: It gives the Osaka nights a car part without breaking rental rules: Pegasis rides as a passenger, and the guide knows where cars gather that week.
cost: passenger tour about 15,000-21,000 JPY per person (US$137 on Viator, €119 on Expedia); MR.HIRO drive 57,000 JPY per car for 1 h
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10; Friday or Saturday nights are best (new-route day 9 is a Wednesday, so move a day if you can). Meets are informal and move; no operator publishes a schedule. Osaka Auto Messe 2027 is Feb 12-14, 2027 at INTEX Osaka: after the trip ends (2026 ticket 3,000 JPY advance).

places.en: Higashi-Osaka PA (Kinki Expressway), known meet spot

experience.hook: Ride shotgun through Osaka's bay area at night and meet local car owners.
moments: Get picked up in the evening and ride along the bay expressways past lit-up port cranes.
Stop where local owners gather that night and talk to them next to their Supras and RX-7s.
Drive past the dark piers of the Tempozan and Nanko area where Osaka's old meets were.
Take night photos with your guide's car under the expressway lights.
experience.tip: Book a Friday or Saturday night. Ask the guide which spot is open that week: PAs close without notice.

title: Fly Kansai to Sapporo on LCC
titleJa: 関西空港→新千歳空港（Peach・ジェットスター）
summary: The cheapest way north: Peach (8 flights a day, 7:20-17:45) or Jetstar (9:50) from Kansai Airport to New Chitose, 1 h 55 min, from 7,110 JPY on Jan 28, 2027. Take the Rapi:t from Namba (about 38 min, 1,670 JPY) and add a checked bag when you book.
why: It is under half the price of JAL/ANA, has flights all day, and KIX is 40 minutes from Namba where the Osaka days end.
cost: Google Flights Jan 28, 2027 (seen Sep 2026): Jetstar 9:50 7,110 JPY; Peach 12:35/16:15/17:45 7,850 JPY, 7:20/10:00/13:55 9,050 JPY. Checked bag: Jetstar 15 kg 2,030-2,500 JPY at booking (2,990+ later), skis +2,500; Peach about 2,000 JPY web / 3,100 airport (2025). Rapi:t 1,670 JPY
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Schedules for Jan 2027 are open. Snow at New Chitose can delay or cancel flights; LCCs rebook only on their own (few) flights, so take a morning flight. Peach uses KIX Terminal 2 (free bus from Terminal 1, allow 20 min extra). JAL also flies KIX-CTS (9:45, 15:30, 13,250-16,550 JPY).

experience.hook: Blue Rapi:t train to the sea airport, two hours later you land in snow.
moments: Ride the blue, round-nosed Rapi:t from Namba across the bridge to the airport island.
Check in at Peach's Terminal 2 and weigh your bag: the 7 kg carry-on limit is strict.
Look down at the Japan Alps and the white north of Honshu from the window.
Land at New Chitose and eat Hokkaido ramen or soft-serve in the domestic terminal.
experience.tip: Buy the checked bag when you book, not later: on Jetstar it costs about 1,000 yen more after booking.

title: Fly Itami to Sapporo (JAL/ANA)
titleJa: 伊丹空港→新千歳空港（JAL・ANA）
summary: Itami is the city airport, 25-35 minutes by limousine bus from Osaka station or Namba (730 JPY). JAL (7:35, 11:45, 15:00, 18:20, from 13,030 JPY on Jan 28, 2027) and ANA (about 7 flights, 8:30-19:05) fly to New Chitose in 1 h 45-50 min, with a 20 kg bag free.
why: Less travel time than KIX, a free bag, and more flights to rebook onto if Hokkaido snow cancels one.
cost: JAL 13,030 JPY (7:35, 11:45, 15:00, 18:20), 16,330 JPY (10:50, 12:45); ANA price not shown on Google Flights, usually similar: check ana.co.jp. Limousine bus 730 JPY
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Jan 2027 schedules open. Snow delays at New Chitose are common, but JAL/ANA have many flights to change to. For East Hokkaido: JAL via CTS to Memanbetsu (7:35 or 11:45 start) 18,240 JPY; no winter nonstop from Osaka to Kushiro.

experience.hook: The easy airport: bus from Umeda, big-airline seat, bag free.
moments: Take the limousine bus from Osaka Station and watch planes land low over the houses near Itami.
Walk through Itami's new terminal, with shops for last Osaka snacks like 551 pork buns.
Fly north over the Sea of Japan coast and see snow start below Tohoku.
Land at New Chitose and pick up the rental car or the rapid train to Sapporo.
experience.tip: Take the 7:35 or 11:45 JAL: a morning flight leaves room to rebook if snow closes New Chitose later.

title: Fly Kobe to Sapporo on Skymark
titleJa: 神戸空港→新千歳空港（スカイマーク・AIRDO）
summary: Kobe Airport, on an island 18 minutes from Sannomiya by Port Liner (340 JPY), has Skymark (8:05, 9:00, 15:05, 17:25), AIRDO (10:30, 19:00) and ANA (8:40) to New Chitose, 1 h 50 min, from 9,070 JPY. Skymark and AIRDO include a 20 kg bag.
why: Nearly LCC prices with a free checked bag, and it fits well if you spend the last Kansai night in Kobe (beef, harbor lights) instead of Osaka.
duration: about 4 h door to door from Osaka
cost: Skymark 17:25 9,070 JPY, 15:05 11,470 JPY, 8:05/9:00 12,570 JPY; AIRDO 10:30 9,965 JPY (Jan 28, 2027). Umeda to Kobe Airport by train about 700 JPY, about 1 h
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Schedules open. Kobe Airport is small and fast: check-in 20 min before is often enough, but Skymark has fewer flights to rebook onto after a snow cancellation.

experience.hook: A small island airport, a free suitcase, and near-LCC prices.
moments: Ride the driverless Port Liner from Sannomiya over the harbor to the airport island.
Check in at a quiet terminal with short lines, then look back at the Rokko mountains.
Fly Skymark with your 20 kg suitcase included in the fare.
Land at New Chitose in the afternoon and drive into the snow.
experience.tip: The 17:25 Skymark (9,070 yen) is cheapest but lands at 19:15 in the dark; plan a Sapporo or Chitose hotel that night.

title: Fly Itami straight to Asahikawa
titleJa: 伊丹空港→旭川空港（JAL）
summary: One JAL nonstop a day, 8:45 to 10:30 (1 h 45 min, 18,960 JPY on Jan 28, 2027), lands you next to Biei and Furano. Start Hokkaido with the Blue Pond, Asahiyama Zoo and Furano skiing, then drive west to Sapporo and fly home from New Chitose.
why: It skips the 2-hour drive from Sapporo to the snow country and gives a clean one-way route through Hokkaido, ending near the international airport.
duration: flight 1 h 45 min; changes the Hokkaido order
cost: 18,960 JPY (JAL, Jan 28, 2027); rental car one-way Asahikawa to New Chitose adds a drop fee
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Only one nonstop (8:45), so leave Osaka hotel by about 7:00. Asahikawa Airport handles snow well but can still close in storms. There is no nonstop from Kansai Airport (Jetstar only via Narita).

experience.hook: Breakfast in Osaka, the Blue Pond in snow before lunch.
moments: Take the early bus to Itami and board the only nonstop to Asahikawa at 8:45.
Land at 10:30 at a small airport in white fields, 20 minutes from Biei.
Drive to the Blue Pond and Shirahige Falls the same afternoon.
Ski Furano the next day, then drive west to Sapporo for the last nights.
experience.tip: Book the rental car at Asahikawa Airport with return at New Chitose; compare the one-way fee with a Sapporo return.

title: Fly Itami to Hakodate
titleJa: 伊丹空港→函館空港（JAL・ANA）
summary: Three nonstops a day: ANA 8:20, JAL 11:10 (17,930 JPY on Jan 28, 2027) and ANA 15:30, about 1 h 30 min. Start Hokkaido in Hakodate (night view, morning market, Love Live Saint Snow places), then drive Onuma, Niseko, Otaru, Sapporo like the old baseline.
why: It keeps the good south-to-north Hokkaido road trip of the first plan without the long Shinkansen from Tokyo.
cost: JAL 11:10 17,930 JPY; ANA 8:20 and 15:30 price not shown on Google Flights (check ana.co.jp)
winterNote: New route day 10 or 11. Schedules open. No flights from Kansai Airport to Hakodate. Hakodate is milder than inland Hokkaido; roads to Niseko are snowy.

experience.hook: From Osaka to Hakodate's famous night view in one afternoon.
moments: Fly the 11:10 JAL and land in Hakodate by 12:40.
Eat a seafood bowl near the morning market or a Lucky Pierrot burger for lunch.
Ride the ropeway up Mt Hakodate for the night view of the narrow lit city.
Drive north the next day past frozen Onuma lake toward Niseko.
experience.tip: Take the 11:10 JAL: you land before lunch and can see the Mt Hakodate view at dusk (about 16:40).

title: Tokaido anime and car road west
titleJa: 東海道 聖地巡礼＆クルマ旅（富士→浜松→名古屋→鈴鹿→京都）
summary: A westward route that puts anime spots and car places on the same days, with the days put in order to fit each place's closed days. D5 (Sat Jan 23) Kawaguchiko → Yuru Camp drive: Motosu, Minobu (Motosu High School model), Fujinomiya · train to Hamamatsu, gyoza dinner · D6 (Sun Jan 24) Suzuki History Museum (weekend = open all day), Yamaha Communication Plaza in Iwata, Mitsuke Tenjin, sunset at the Bentenjima torii (Yuru Camp S2 ep 3), train to Nagoya · D7 (Mon Jan 25) Suzuka Circuit: drive an EV kart on the real F1 East Course, evening Osu (Medalist) · D8 (Tue Jan 26) Toyota Commemorative Museum + Toyota Kaikan, evening train to Kyoto · D9 (Wed Jan 27) Omi Jingu (Chihayafuru) + Demachi (Tamako Market, Eccentric Family) · D10 (Thu Jan 28) Uji (Euphonium, KyoAni monument) + Nishinomiya (Haruhi), fly Itami → Sapporo in the evening or on D11.
why: It is one line of travel with no going back, and every day has both an anime place and a car place, which is what both of them like most.
cost: Trains approx 16,000 JPY per person Mishima/Fuji → Kyoto in parts; Suzuka entry 2,000–2,400 + EV kart 2,000 per kart; museums 0–1,000 JPY each; rental car on D5 approx 8,000–12,000 JPY/day
winterNote: New route day 5–10. The order matters: Suzuka Circuit is CLOSED Jan 12–21 and Jan 26–29, 2027 (open Jan 22–25), so Suzuka must be D5–D7. Toyota Commemorative Museum is closed Mondays (Jan 25), Toyota Kaikan is closed Sundays, Suzuki History Museum is closed Mondays and on weekdays from Sep to Jan lets normal visitors in only from 15:00. D5 roads near Motosu can be icy: winter tyres, Aoki drives.

places.en: Bentenjima seaside park torii (Yuru Camp S2)

places.ja: トヨタ産業技術記念館

anime: Yuru Camp (S1, S2 ep 2–3), Medalist, Chihayafuru, Tamako Market, The Eccentric Family, Sound! Euphonium, Haruhi Suzumiya

experience.hook: Six days west: anime towns in the morning, race cars and car factories in the afternoon.
moments: Eat a Minobu manju at Minobu Station, the small town where Nadeshiko lives in Yuru Camp.
Watch the sun go down behind the red torii in Lake Hamana, as Rin does in Yuru Camp S2.
Drive an EV kart through the first corners of the Suzuka F1 East Course.
See Toyota's first looms and a line of car-building robots at the museum in Nagoya.
Climb the Haruhi hill in Nishinomiya, then fly north to the snow.
experience.tip: Book the Suzuka EV kart online (Asoview) as soon as the January slots open; the ticket window does not sell it.
