title: Yuru Camp west: Minobu, Fujinomiya
titleJa: ゆるキャン△ 身延・富士宮 聖地巡礼
summary: Leave Kawaguchiko to the west instead of going back to Tokyo: past Lake Motosu to Kai-Tokiwa Station and the old Shimobe school (model of Motosu High School), then Minobu Station street and Minobu manju. Go south to Fujinomiya: Fujisan Hongu Sengen Taisha and Fujinomiya yakisoba (S2 ep 7), then the Tokaido line at Fuji.
why: It turns the Fuji days into the start of the trip west, with the home town of Nadeshiko and Rin that the covered Motosu campsite stop does not show.
duration: 1 day (by car, or JR Minobu line)
cost: Rental car approx 8,000–12,000 JPY/day, or JR Minobu line approx 1,500 JPY; manju approx 80 JPY each; yakisoba approx 700 JPY
winterNote: New route day 5 (Kawaguchiko → Tokaido). The school model (旧下部小・中学校) can be seen only from outside. It opens inside only at events (e.g. Nov 28, 2026); no January 2027 event is announced. Route 300 past Motosu can be icy in the morning: winter tyres. JR Minobu line trains are about 1 per hour.
anime: Yuru Camp: Motosu High School commute (S1 ep 8), Minobu manju, Fujinomiya (S2 ep 7), Asagiri Kogen soft cream (S1 ep 3)

experience.hook: The quiet valley town where the Outdoor Activities Club goes to school.
moments: Walk the 600 m from Kai-Tokiwa Station over the small river to the old wooden-looking school, Motosu High in the show.
Buy warm Minobu manju at Eisho-do near Minobu Station, as the girls do.
Stop at Asagiri Kogen road station for a milk soft cream with Fuji right behind it.
Stand at the red torii of Hongu Sengen Taisha, then eat Fujinomiya yakisoba nearby.
experience.tip: Go to Asagiri Kogen before 10:00; the Fuji view is clearest in the morning before clouds come.

title: Yuru Camp S2: Rin's New Year trip
titleJa: ゆるキャン△ SEASON2 浜名湖・御前崎 聖地巡礼
summary: In Yuru Camp Season 2 ep 1–3, Rin rides west over New Year: Omaezaki Lighthouse, Kakezuka Lighthouse, Mitsuke Tenjin in Iwata, the Nagisaen campsite and the red torii at Bentenjima on Lake Hamana, Kanzanji Onsen and the Okuhamanako lookout. Stop in Hamamatsu for a half or full day on the way to Nagoya.
why: The story happens in late December and January, so the winter light and cold wind match what they will see.
duration: half day (Bentenjima, Kanzanji) to 1 day (with Omaezaki, by car)
cost: Local trains approx 1,000 JPY; Hamamatsu gyoza approx 1,000 JPY; eel bowl approx 4,000–6,000 JPY
winterNote: New route day 5 or 6. Mild coast, no snow; strong dry west wind in January. Bentenjima torii is best at sunset (about 17:15 in late Jan). Omaezaki is far from the train: needs a car.

places.ja: 見付天神 矢奈比賣神社

anime: Yuru Camp SEASON 2 ep 1–3 (Rin's solo New Year trip to west Shizuoka, Nadeshiko's grandmother by Lake Hamana)

experience.hook: Follow Rin's New Year scooter trip, in the same cold January light.
moments: Climb the white Omaezaki Lighthouse and look at the Pacific, where Rin starts Season 2.
Walk the stone steps of Mitsuke Tenjin in Iwata, seen when Rin looks for places to go.
Watch the red torii at Bentenjima turn black against the sunset over Lake Hamana.
Eat Hamamatsu gyoza in a ring with bean sprouts in the middle for dinner.
experience.tip: Combine with Yamaha Communication Plaza: Mitsuke Tenjin and the plaza are both in Iwata, a short taxi apart.

title: Hamamatsu: Suzuki, Yamaha, Honda roots
titleJa: 浜松・磐田 ものづくりの街（スズキ歴史館・ヤマハ発動機コミュニケーションプラザ）
summary: Hamamatsu is where Suzuki, Yamaha and Honda started. See the free Suzuki History Museum (looms from 1909, old cars and bikes, how cars are made today; book ahead) and Yamaha Motor's free Communication Plaza in Iwata (racing bikes, engines; renewed June 2026). With a car, add the Honda Soichiro Monozukuri museum in Tenryu.
why: It is JDM history for free and fits on the Tokaido line between Fuji and Nagoya.
cost: Free entry at both museums; local trains approx 500 JPY
winterNote: New route day 6 (Sun Jan 24) is best. Suzuki History Museum: reservation only, closed Mondays; Sep–Jan weekdays are for school trips, so normal visitors only from 15:00 on weekdays. Bookings open about 2 months ahead (Nov 2026 for January). Yamaha plaza: free, no booking for groups up to 10; open on company workdays 9:00–17:00 and some weekend days 10:00–17:00; check its calendar. In 2025 guides said a Toyota 2000GT (engine by Yamaha) was shown; not checked after the 2026 renewal. Honda museum (Tenryu) is closed Mon–Tue.

places.ja: ヤマハ発動機 コミュニケーションプラザ

experience.hook: One city gave the world Suzuki, Yamaha and Honda. Both museums are free.
moments: Walk past Michio Suzuki's 1909 wooden loom, then the first Suzuki cars and bikes.
See a real car shown in parts at the Suzuki museum's production floor.
Look at Yamaha's MotoGP bikes and marine engines at the new Iwata plaza.
Eat a Hamamatsu eel bowl or gyoza between the two museums.
experience.tip: Book the Suzuki museum for a Saturday or Sunday; on weekdays in January you can only go in after 15:00.

title: Suzuka Circuit: drive the F1 track
titleJa: 鈴鹿サーキット サーキットチャレンジャー
summary: Suzuka Circuit, home of the Japanese F1 GP, has a park where anyone can drive an EV kart on the real racing course (East Course) with no licence needed. Walk the grandstand and the pit side, and see the Honda race cars on show.
why: Pegasis cannot rent a car with 1 year of licence, but here both of them can drive on an F1 track.
cost: Entry 2,000–2,400 JPY adult (web is 500 JPY less), EV kart 2,000 JPY per kart (up to 3 people)
winterNote: New route day 5–7 ONLY. Official: closed Jan 12–21 and Jan 26–29, 2027 for checks, so it is open Jan 22–25 (Fri–Mon). Winter hours about 10:00–16:30. Circuit Challenger tickets are online only (Asoview), not at the gate. No race events found for these dates. Honda's Suzuka car plant nearby had weekday tours (8:50, 13:45, free, booking) per a tour list; not confirmed for individuals or 2027.

experience.hook: No licence needed: you drive the real Suzuka F1 East Course yourself.
moments: Drive the EV kart through turn 1 and the S-curves on the real F1 tarmac.
Stand on the main grandstand and look down the pit straight.
See the race cars and bikes on show in the park plaza.
Eat a hot lunch at the circuit restaurants on a cold, clear winter day.
experience.tip: Buy entry on the web (500 JPY less) and book the first kart slot; afternoons can be windy and cold.

title: Toyota day: Commemorative Museum, Kaikan
titleJa: トヨタ産業技術記念館・トヨタ会館
summary: Start at the Toyota Commemorative Museum by Nagoya Station, in Toyota's first red-brick loom factory: looms, then cars built step by step with robot demos. Then go to Toyota City for the free Toyota Kaikan Museum by the head office, with new Toyota, Lexus and GAZOO Racing cars and a new 'how Toyota builds cars' area (June 2026).
why: It adds the factory side of Toyota to the covered Toyota Automobile Museum, and both are easy by train.
cost: Commemorative Museum 1,000 JPY; Toyota Kaikan free; trains approx 1,500 JPY
winterNote: New route day 8 (Tue Jan 26) fits: the Commemorative Museum is closed Mondays (Jan 25), Toyota Kaikan is closed Sundays. Real plant tours at Toyota City stay stopped (notice 2023, still up in 2026); only the virtual tour runs. Toyota Kaikan museum guided tour now starts at 14:30.

places.en: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
places.ja: トヨタ産業技術記念館

photoQuery: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology

experience.hook: From wooden looms to GR race cars, in Toyota's own home town.
moments: Hear the old looms run in the red-brick hall where Toyota began.
Watch a car body go from pressed steel to welded shell in the automobile hall.
Ride the Meitetsu train to Toyota City and see the GAZOO Racing corner at Toyota Kaikan.
Buy GR and Lexus model cars in the Toyota Kaikan shop.
experience.tip: Do the Commemorative Museum at 9:30 opening, then Toyota Kaikan in the afternoon to join the 14:30 tour.

title: Nagoya: Medalist rink and Osu
titleJa: メダリスト 聖地巡礼 大須（名古屋スポーツセンター）
summary: The figure skating anime Medalist (S2 aired Jan 2026) is set in Nagoya. Skate at the real home rink of Inori's club, Osu Skating Rink, see Osu Kannon and the Fuji-shaped slide at Uramonzen park (taiyaki scene, ep 3), and walk Osu shopping street, also used in Yatogame-chan. Near Nagoya Station, Coffee House Kako is Rin's breakfast cafe in the Yuru Camp movie.
why: Skating in winter where the anime was drawn is fun for both, and Osu is Nagoya's otaku and food street.
cost: Skating 1,500 JPY + skate rental 500 JPY; Osu street food approx 1,500 JPY
winterNote: New route day 6–8. Osu rink public hours: weekdays 12:00–18:00, weekends 10:00–18:00; closed only Jan 1 (it can be booked out for events; check the site). Wear gloves on the ice.

places.ja: 名古屋スポーツセンター（大須スケートリンク）

anime: Medalist (Lux Higashiyama FSC home rink, Osu Kannon, taiyaki park ep 3); Yatogame-chan (Osu); Yuru Camp movie (Rin's cafe in Nagoya)

experience.hook: Skate on the real rink where Inori trains in Medalist.
moments: Slide down past the stair handrail from Medalist ep 1, then rent skates and go on the ice.
Drink coffee in the rink's Komeda, drawn as 'Yoneda Coffee' in the anime.
Eat taiyaki on a bench at Uramonzen park by the big Fuji-shaped slide.
Walk the covered Osu streets for retro games, figures and fried chicken.
experience.tip: The rink has signed photos and real skates of Mao Asada and Shoma Uno in its gallery corner; look before you skate.

title: Chihayafuru: Omi Jingu, Otsu
titleJa: ちはやふる 聖地 近江神宮
summary: Omi Jingu in Otsu is the 'holy place' of competitive karuta and the key place of Chihayafuru: the Meijin and Queen title matches are held every January in its Omi Kangakudo hall. Walk the vermilion gate and shrine, and see the clock museum with about 2,300 clocks.
why: It is 10 minutes from Kyoto by train and is one of the big anime places in Kansai that the old plan did not have.
cost: Shrine free; clock museum small fee; train from Kyoto approx 200–400 JPY
winterNote: New route day 9. The 2026 Meijin/Queen matches were on Jan 10–11, before this trip; 2027 dates not yet announced but likely early January too. Omi Kangakudo is a working hall: outside only when there is no event.
anime: Chihayafuru (Omi Jingu, national karuta tournaments and title matches)

experience.hook: The shrine where Chihaya dreams of becoming Queen of karuta.
moments: Walk up the long approach to the bright vermilion tower gate from the anime.
See the Omi Kangakudo hall where the real Meijin and Queen matches happen each January.
Look at the old water clock and 2,300 clocks in the museum by the shrine.
Buy a karuta-themed omamori or ema at the shrine office.
experience.tip: Take the Keihan Ishiyama-Sakamoto line to Omi-Jingu-mae; it is a short walk and quieter than JR Otsukyo.

title: Demachi: Tamako Market, Eccentric Family
titleJa: 出町桝形商店街・下鴨神社（たまこまーけっと／有頂天家族）
summary: Demachi Masugata shopping street in Kyoto is the model for Usagiyama street in KyoAni's Tamako Market: find the mackerel object, the Tamako pictures and the fan notebook. Cross the Kamo river delta to Shimogamo Shrine and Tadasu no Mori, where the tanuki family lives in The Eccentric Family.
why: Two well-loved Kyoto anime in a 1-hour walk, with mochi and a winter forest.
cost: Free; mame-mochi at Demachi Futaba approx 250 JPY
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. City spots, open all year. Some shops in the arcade close on Tuesdays or at irregular days; Demachi Futaba often has a queue.

places.en: Demachi Futaba (Tamaya model, said by fans)

anime: Tamako Market / Tamako Love Story (Usagiyama shopping street, Kamo river); The Eccentric Family (Shimogamo tanuki in Tadasu no Mori, Demachi arcade in ep 1)

experience.hook: Tamako's mochi street and the tanuki forest, one river apart.
moments: Find the big mackerel object hanging in the middle of Masugata arcade.
Write a note in the Tamako Market fan notebook in the arcade.
Eat mame-mochi from Demachi Futaba while you cross the Kamo river stepping stones.
Walk into Tadasu no Mori, home of the Shimogamo tanuki in The Eccentric Family.
experience.tip: Go before 10:00: the Futaba line is short, and the stepping stones at the delta have fewer people.

title: Uji deeper: KyoAni, Euphonium, Medalist
titleJa: 宇治 深掘り（志を繋ぐ碑・ユーフォ聖地・木下アカデミー京都アイスアリーナ）
summary: Beyond Uji Bridge and Daikichiyama (already in the list): Kumiko's bench on Ajirogi path, Agata Shrine, Asagiri Bridge and Keihan Uji Station from Sound! Euphonium. Visit the KyoAni 'monument that links hopes' in the Tea and Uji history park, and the Kyoto Ice Arena used for the Rengecha club in Medalist.
why: It adds a quiet moment for Kyoto Animation, whose shows they like, and more Uji scenes on the same half day.
cost: Free; history park museum 800 JPY (optional)
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10. History park open 9:00–17:00, no regular closed day, park is free. The city asks visitors not to leave flowers or offerings at the monument. There is no fixed KyoAni Shop store now (only pop-up shops at events). Keihan × Euphonium collab ends Dec 20, 2026.

places.en: Tea and Uji history park (KyoAni monument)
places.ja: お茶と宇治のまち歴史公園（志を繋ぐ碑）
木下アカデミー京都アイスアリーナ

anime: Sound! Euphonium (Kumiko bench, Agata Shrine, Asagiri Bridge); Kyoto Animation memorial monument; Medalist (Rengecha FSC home rink)

experience.hook: Kumiko's river walk, and a quiet stop for the people of Kyoto Animation.
moments: Sit on Kumiko's bench on the Ajirogi path by the Uji river.
Cross the red Asagiri Bridge to the island, as in the Euphonium opening.
Stand for a quiet minute at the monument with 36 birds in the history park.
Look at the Kyoto Ice Arena where Medalist's Rengecha skaters train.
experience.tip: Buy matcha soft serve on Byodoin Omotesando after the walk; lines are short on January weekdays.

title: Haruhi: Nishinomiya's last winter
titleJa: 涼宮ハルヒの憂鬱 聖地巡礼 西宮（西宮北高校・甲陽園）
summary: Nishinomiya is the town of Haruhi Suzumiya. See the Nishinomiya-Kitaguchi Station area (Endless Eight), take the Hankyu line to Koyoen, walk past Yuki Nagato's apartment area and climb the steep 'Haruhi hill' to Nishinomiya Kita High School, North High in the anime.
why: The school closes as 'Nishinomiya Kita' at the end of March 2027, so this is the last winter to see the real North High.
cost: Hankyu trains approx 400 JPY; cafe approx 700 JPY
winterNote: New route day 10, on the way to Itami Airport (20 min by bus/train). Official Haruhi site: the school merges and becomes Nishinomiya Kurakuen High School after March 2027. School is outside only (the Nov 23, 2025 open day was a one-time event). The hill is steep: 20–25 min up. Coffee-ya Dream (Endless Eight cafe) posts hours 8:00–18:00 on X; it may have moved, check before going.

places.ja: 兵庫県立西宮北高等学校

anime: The Melancholy of Haruhi Suzumiya (North High and the school hill, Endless Eight, Koyoen = 'Koyoen' station)

experience.hook: Climb the Haruhi hill before North High changes its name in 2027.
moments: Stand at the Haruhi-famous clock area of Nishinomiya-Kitaguchi Station.
Ride the short Hankyu Koyo line to the small Koyoen terminus.
Walk up the steep hill to North High, the daily climb Kyon complains about.
Look back from the top over Nishinomiya to Osaka Bay.
experience.tip: Go on a weekend or after 16:00 on weekdays; it is a real school, so do not film students or go inside the gate.

title: Mazda Museum day from Osaka
titleJa: マツダミュージアム（広島）
summary: A free guided tour at Mazda's home in Hiroshima: rotary engines, the RX-7 line, the 787B Le Mans winner, and a view of a real assembly line. From Osaka it is a day trip: Shinkansen to Hiroshima (about 1 h 25), then 5 min to Mukainada.
why: Rotary RX-7s are JDM icons, and it is the only big car-maker tour open to walk-in tourists on this route; Hiroshima okonomiyaki is a bonus.
cost: Tour free; Shin-Osaka–Hiroshima Shinkansen approx 10,000–11,000 JPY each way
winterNote: New route day 9 or 10 (weekdays only; no weekend tours). One English tour a day (meet 14:15 at the head office lobby, shuttle bus). Book online, up to 3 months ahead (from late Oct 2026). Museum closed Feb 8–26, 2027 for works (after this trip). It is far: only if they want a big car day.

experience.hook: See the rotary engine story and a real Mazda line, free.
moments: Ride the Mazda shuttle bus from the head office into the huge plant.
Stand next to the 787B, the only Japanese car to win Le Mans in 1991.
Walk past the rotary cars, from the Cosmo Sport to the RX-7.
Watch workers and robots build real cars on the assembly line.
Eat Hiroshima okonomiyaki with noodles before the train back.
experience.tip: Book the English slot the day the 3-month window opens; weekday slots are few.

title: Toyota Hokkaido plant tour, Tomakomai
titleJa: トヨタ自動車北海道 工場見学（苫小牧）
summary: Toyota's Hokkaido factory in Tomakomai, about 30 min by car from New Chitose Airport, makes automatic and CVT gearboxes. The free 90-minute tour shows people and robots working side by side.
why: The Toyota City plant tours are stopped, so this is the real Toyota factory they can see, and it is on the way from the airport.
cost: Free
winterNote: New route day 11 (Fri Jan 29) or day 14 (Mon Feb 1): tours run Mon–Fri and on holidays, not weekends. Two slots a day (10:00 and an afternoon slot; sources say 13:00 or 14:00). Book on the official booking site 6 months to 3 weeks ahead (so by early January). Tour is in Japanese; individual visitors are allowed according to visitor reports, but confirm when booking. Needs a car (no near station).

experience.hook: The one Toyota factory you can still walk through on this trip.
moments: Drive from New Chitose Airport over the flat, snowy Yufutsu plain.
Walk the tour path above the line where CVT gearboxes are built.
Watch robots hand parts to workers at speed.
Pick up Toyota Hokkaido souvenirs at the end.
experience.tip: Book the 10:00 slot on the day you land or leave, so the plant fits between the airport and Sapporo.

title: West route A: Tokaido line
titleJa: 東海道ルート：東京・富士・沼津・名古屋・京都・大阪・北海道
summary: D1 Tue Jan 19 land Narita, Skyliner to Shinjuku (1 h 23 min, ¥2,820) · D2 Tokyo anime day (Suga shrine, Nakano, Akihabara) · D3 Kawasaki (Girls Band Cry) + guided Daikoku PA night · D4 highway bus Shinjuku→Kawaguchiko (~2 h), Oishi Park and lake, sleep Kawaguchiko · D5 Sat Chureito Pagoda at sunrise, Mishima-Kawaguchiko Liner bus to Mishima (1 h 43 min, ¥2,700), Numazu Love Live! Sunshine!! spots (Awashima, Uchiura), sleep Numazu · D6 Sun Hikari Mishima→Nagoya (1 h 15 min, ¥8,440), afternoon Toyota Automobile Museum (open Sun, closed Mon), sleep Nagoya · D7 Mon Ghibli Park (closed Tue), evening Shinkansen Nagoya→Kyoto (34 min, ¥5,910) · D8 Tue Kyoto: Fushimi Inari early, Kiyomizu, Gion · D9 Wed Uji (Euphonium) + Nara deer and Todaiji · D10 Thu Kyoto→Osaka: Kinkakuji in the morning, Dotonbori night, sleep Namba · D11 Fri Jan 29 Nankai to KIX, Jetstar 9:50→11:50 New Chitose, rental car, drive to Niseko (~2 h) · D12 Sat Niseko ski (Pegasis) / lesson (Aoki) · D13 Sun ski morning, drive to Otaru (~1 h 30 min), canal at night · D14 Mon Otaru→Sapporo, ramen, see snow-festival statues being built at Odori · D15 Tue Feb 2 CTS: Aoki flies Spring 13:50 direct to Shanghai, Pegasis flies Air Canada evening to Vancouver→Toronto. Nights: Tokyo 3, Kawaguchiko 1, Numazu 1, Nagoya 1, Kyoto 3, Osaka 1, Niseko 2, Otaru 1, Sapporo 1. Hokkaido = 4 nights, 4.5 days.
why: Most variety for the west part: Fuji sunrise, two anime towns (Numazu, Uji), cars (Daikoku, Toyota museum) and Ghibli, and each travel day is short.
cost: Transport approx ¥65,000–80,000 per person: Skyliner ¥2,820 · Tokyo trains ~¥3,000 · bus to Kawaguchiko ~¥2,200–2,600 · Mishima Liner ¥2,700 · Numazu buses ~¥1,500 · Hikari Mishima→Nagoya ¥8,440 · Nagoya subway + Linimo 2 days ~¥2,000 · Nagoya→Kyoto ¥5,910 · Kansai Mini Pass ¥3,000 (3 days, JR local) + Kintetsu/extra ~¥1,000 · Nankai to KIX ¥970 · Jetstar/Peach KIX→CTS ¥7,000–10,000 + checked bag ~¥2,500–4,000 · Hokkaido 4WD car 4 days + fuel + tolls, split by 2, ~¥27,000–32,000 (car price approx, not checked). No JR pass: single tickets are cheaper.
winterNote: Ghibli Park closes on Tuesdays; January 2027 tickets go on sale Nov 10, 2026, 14:00 JST (sale is 2 months ahead on the 10th). Toyota Automobile Museum closes Mondays. Wakakusa Yamayaki (Nara, Sat Jan 23, 2027, fireworks 18:15, fire 18:30) falls on D5, so this version misses it. Sapporo Snow Festival 2027 is Feb 4–11 and Otaru Snow Light Path Feb 6–13: both start after the trip ends Feb 2. Chureito sunrise needs a clear morning; Fuji is often clear in January.
anime: Love Live! Sunshine!! (Numazu, Awashima, Uchiura), Hibike! Euphonium (Uji), Ghibli films (Ghibli Park), Girls Band Cry (Kawasaki)

experience.hook: Fuji sunrise, a Love Live seaside town, Ghibli, Kyoto, then Hokkaido powder.
moments: Stand at Chureito Pagoda at sunrise with red pagoda, snow-capped Fuji and frozen breath in one photo.
Walk the Uchiura seafront in Numazu and look across the bay to Awashima, Aqours' island.
Stand next to a Toyota 2000GT at the Toyota Automobile Museum, then walk Ghibli's Grand Warehouse the next day.
Climb Fushimi Inari's orange gates at 7:00 before the crowds, then eat matcha soft cream by Uji Bridge.
Land at New Chitose at noon and be on Niseko snow the same evening, with Yotei in view.
experience.tip: Put Nagoya on Sunday–Monday: the car museum closes Mondays and Ghibli Park closes Tuesdays.

title: West route B: Alps and Hokuriku
titleJa: アルプス・北陸ルート：松本・高山・白川郷・金沢・京都・北海道
summary: D1 Tue Jan 19 land Narita, Skyliner to Shinjuku · D2 Tokyo anime day · D3 Kawasaki + Daikoku PA night · D4 Fri Fuji day trip by bus (Kawaguchiko, Chureito) or Hakone, back to Tokyo · D5 Sat Azusa Shinjuku→Matsumoto (2 h 39 min, ¥6,730), Matsumoto Castle in snow, sleep Matsumoto · D6 Sun Jan 24 bus Matsumoto→Takayama (about 2 h 30 min, ~¥4,000–4,500), Takayama old town (Hyouka), evening Shirakawa-go light-up bus tour from Takayama (returns the same night) · D7 Mon morning train to Hida-Furukawa (Your Name), afternoon Nohi bus Takayama→Kanazawa via Shirakawa-go (~2 h 30 min, ~¥4,200), sleep Kanazawa · D8 Tue Kenrokuen + Omicho market, afternoon Tsurugi Shinkansen + Thunderbird via Tsuruga to Kyoto (2 h 4 min, ¥7,720) · D9 Wed Kyoto: Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu, Gion · D10 Thu Uji + Nara, sleep Osaka · D11 Fri Jan 29 fly Itami→New Chitose (JAL 11:45→13:30, from ~¥13,000; or Peach from KIX ~¥8,000), rental car, drive to Furano (~2 h 30 min) · D12 Sat Furano ski · D13 Sun Blue Pond + Asahiyama Zoo, sleep Asahikawa · D14 Mon drive to Sapporo (~2 h), return car · D15 Tue Feb 2 fly home from CTS. Nights: Tokyo 4, Matsumoto 1, Takayama 1, Kanazawa 1, Kyoto 2, Osaka 1, Furano 2, Asahikawa 1, Sapporo 1. Hokkaido = 4 nights, 4.5 days.
why: It catches the Shirakawa-go light-up on Sun Jan 24, adds two anime towns (Hyouka, Your Name), a black castle in snow and Furano's dry powder.
cost: Transport approx ¥88,000–105,000 per person incl. the light-up tour: Skyliner ¥2,820 · Tokyo trains ~¥3,000 · Fuji day by bus ~¥4,800 · Azusa ¥6,730 · Matsumoto→Takayama bus ~¥4,000–4,500 · light-up bus tour from Takayama ¥13,000–16,000 · Takayama↔Hida-Furukawa JR ~¥500 · Takayama→Kanazawa bus ~¥4,200 · Kanazawa→Kyoto ¥7,720 · Kansai trains ~¥4,000 · Itami access ~¥700 · ITM→CTS ¥13,000–17,000 (JAL/ANA, bag included) · Hokkaido car 4 days split by 2 ~¥27,000–32,000 (approx). No pass pays off: the Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass (¥19,800, 5 days) covers only ~¥13,000 of these legs.
winterNote: Shirakawa-go light-up 2027: Jan 11, 17, 24, 31, 17:30–19:30, reservation only; Nohi bus tours from Takayama go on sale Oct 13–Nov 2, 2026 (staggered). One nonstop Itami→Asahikawa exists (JAL, 8:45, about ¥19,000 on Jan 28, 2027 per Google Flights; see rw4-fly-itm-asahikawa); it saves the 2 h 30 min drive to Furano but costs more than CTS. Asahiyama Zoo winter hours 10:30–15:30. Wakakusa Yamayaki (Sat Jan 23) and Sapporo Snow Festival (Feb 4–11, 2027) are both missed. Hokkaido roads: 4WD + studless tyres, drive in daylight.
anime: Hyouka (Takayama), Your Name (Hida-Furukawa), Hibike! Euphonium (Uji)

experience.hook: Castle, thatched village lit at night, then Hokkaido's driest powder.
moments: Walk across the red bridge to Matsumoto Castle, black walls against fresh snow.
Stand on the Shiroyama deck on Sun Jan 24 as the thatched roofs of Shirakawa-go light up below.
Wait on the Hida-Furukawa platform where Taki arrives in Your Name, then walk the white-walled canal street.
Eat a seafood bowl at Omicho Market, then ride the new Hokuriku Shinkansen to Tsuruga.
Ski Furano's long groomed runs, then see Blue Pond lit up blue in the snow at night.
experience.tip: Book the Takayama light-up bus tour the day sales open in October; Jan 24 tours sell out.

title: West route C: short west, long Hokkaido
titleJa: 関西は短く、北海道を長く
summary: D1 Tue Jan 19 land Narita, Skyliner to Shinjuku · D2 Tokyo anime day · D3 Kawasaki + Daikoku PA night · D4 Fri Fuji day trip by bus (Kawaguchiko, Chureito) · D5 Sat Jan 23 Nozomi Tokyo→Kyoto (2 h 15 min, ¥14,170), Fushimi Inari, evening Kintetsu to Nara (~45 min) for the Wakakusa Yamayaki fireworks 18:15 and hill fire 18:30, sleep Kyoto · D6 Sun Kinkakuji early + Uji (Euphonium) · D7 Mon to Osaka: Osaka Castle, Nipponbashi Den Den Town, Dotonbori, sleep Namba · D8 Tue Jan 26 Nankai to KIX, Jetstar 9:50→11:50 New Chitose, rental car, drive to Otaru (~1 h 15 min), canal at night · D9 Wed drive to Niseko (~2 h), afternoon ski · D10 Thu Niseko ski · D11 Fri Niseko ski / Aoki lesson, onsen · D12 Sat drive to Sapporo (~2 h 30 min), Susukino · D13 Sun drive to Asahikawa (~2 h), Asahiyama Zoo, Blue Pond at night, sleep Asahikawa · D14 Mon back to Sapporo, return car · D15 Tue Feb 2 fly home from CTS. Nights: Tokyo 4, Kyoto 2, Osaka 1, Otaru 1, Niseko 3, Sapporo 2, Asahikawa 1. Hokkaido = 7 nights, 7.5 days.
why: Pegasis gets 3 Niseko ski days and Aoki time to learn, the west part still has Kyoto, Uji and the one-night Nara fire festival.
cost: Transport approx ¥80,000–95,000 per person: Skyliner ¥2,820 · Tokyo trains ~¥3,000 · Fuji day by bus ~¥4,800 · Nozomi Tokyo→Kyoto ¥14,170 (reserved; smartEX ~¥200 less) · Kyoto/Nara/Uji/Osaka trains ~¥4,000 · Nankai to KIX ¥970 · KIX→CTS ¥7,000–10,000 + bag ~¥2,500–4,000 · Hokkaido 4WD car 7 days + fuel + tolls, split by 2, ~¥45,000–55,000 (approx, not checked). Cheaper: no car in Niseko days, JR CTS→Kutchan ¥3,100 (2 h 56 min). No JR pass pays off.
winterNote: Wakakusa Yamayaki 2027: Sat Jan 23 (New route day 5), fireworks 18:15, burning 18:30; best view from Nara Park or Heijo Palace site; last trains back to Kyoto are crowded. Sapporo Snow Festival 2027 is Feb 4–11 and Otaru Snow Light Path Feb 6–13, both after the trip; in late January you can see snow statues being built at Odori. Niseko night skiing runs in winter; snowstorms can close the Otaru–Niseko road (Route 5) for hours.
anime: Hibike! Euphonium (Uji)

experience.hook: A whole hill set on fire in Nara, then a week of Hokkaido snow.
moments: Watch fireworks over Nara, then see the whole grass hill of Wakakusa burn orange at 18:30.
Stand at Kinkakuji at opening time, then sip matcha by Uji Bridge in Euphonium's town.
Walk Otaru canal at night with gas lamps and snow banks, then eat fresh sushi.
Ski three days of Niseko powder under Mt Yotei; Aoki takes a lesson in Hirafu.
Watch penguins walk through the snow at Asahiyama Zoo, then see Blue Pond lit up.
experience.tip: Book the Kyoto hotel near Kintetsu Kyoto station for Jan 23; the Nara trains back fill up after 19:00.

title: JR pass check for west route
titleJa: JRパス比較（西ルート）
summary: No JR pass pays off on any of the three west-route versions; buy single tickets on smartEX (Tokaido Shinkansen) or JR-West online, and use the Kansai Mini Pass (¥3,000, 3 days) in Kyoto/Osaka/Nara. The Nationwide JR Pass is ¥53,000 for 7 days from Oct 1, 2026, but the JR legs on this route cost only about ¥18,000–20,000.
why: It saves about ¥30,000 per person compared with a Nationwide pass that many blogs still recommend.
cost: Nationwide JR Pass 7 days: ¥50,000 until Sep 30, 2026, ¥53,000 from Oct 1, 2026 (+ special ticket for Nozomi, e.g. Tokyo–Shin-Osaka ¥4,960). JR-covered legs per version: A ~¥20,000 (Hikari Mishima→Nagoya ¥8,440, Nagoya→Kyoto ¥5,910, Kansai locals); B ~¥18,000 (Azusa ¥6,730, Kanazawa→Kyoto ¥7,720, locals; buses not JR); C ~¥18,000 (Nozomi Tokyo→Kyoto ¥14,170, locals). Takayama-Hokuriku Area Tourist Pass ¥19,800/5 days covers only ~¥13,000 of B. Kansai-Hokuriku Area Pass ¥19,000/7 days covers ~¥13,000 of B. Kansai-Hiroshima Area Pass ¥17,000/5 days pays only if you add a Hiroshima/Miyajima day.
winterNote: New route days 5–10. JR-West's Kansai Area Pass (1–4 days) stops sales on Sep 30, 2026; the Kansai Mini Pass (¥3,000, 3 days, JR local/rapid only, no Shinkansen, no Haruka) stays. A JR Pass bought now at ¥50,000 cannot be kept until January (exchange orders must be used within 3 months). Tokaido Shinkansen prices change a little by season (late January is often an off-peak day, about ¥200 less).

experience.hook: Add up the tickets first: the big pass loses you ¥30,000.
moments: Book Tokaido Shinkansen seats on smartEX with a foreign credit card, then tap in with the same card or QR.
Check EX Hayatoku 21 fares 21+ days before; some Nozomi seats are cheaper than normal.
Buy the ¥3,000 Kansai Mini Pass for Kyoto, Uji, Nara (JR) and Osaka days.
Use Suica/ICOCA for everything else: buses, subways, Kintetsu.
experience.tip: Many blogs still show the Kansai Area Pass; it stops selling Sep 30, 2026.

title: Skip suitcases: Tokyo to Kyoto
titleJa: 宅急便で荷物を先に送る（東京→京都）
summary: On the west route, send the big suitcases with Yamato from the Tokyo hotel straight to the Kyoto hotel, and travel with a daypack through Fuji, Numazu/Matsumoto, Takayama and Nagoya. At the end, carry them on the plane to Hokkaido (cheaper than sending).
why: Buses to Kawaguchiko, Takayama and Shirakawa-go have little luggage space, and they change hotels 5 times before Kyoto.
cost: Yamato cash price Kanto→Kansai: 120 size ¥2,040, 140 size ¥2,630, 160 size ¥3,020 (¥100 less if you bring it to a shop). Kansai→Hokkaido: 140 ¥3,810, 160 ¥4,180. A checked bag on Peach/Jetstar costs about ¥2,500–4,000, JAL/ANA includes 20 kg.
winterNote: New route: send on D3 or D4 from Tokyo, it arrives in Kyoto the next day or the day after. Ask the Kyoto hotel to keep it. Existing idea 'deal-yamato-suitcase-sapporo' covers Tokyo→Sapporo; on this route Kyoto is the better target because you fly from Osaka with the bags anyway. Snow can delay Hokkaido deliveries by a day.

experience.hook: Five towns in five days with only a daypack.
moments: Hand the suitcase to the Shinjuku hotel desk and fill in one Yamato form.
Climb onto the Kawaguchiko or Takayama bus with no fight for luggage space.
Open your Kyoto hotel room and find the suitcase waiting.
experience.tip: Measure the case: height + width + depth over 160 cm jumps to the 180 size price.

title: Fly in Narita, out Sapporo
titleJa: 成田着・新千歳発のオープンジョー
summary: Book each person's flights as multi-city: arrive Narita/Haneda Jan 19, leave New Chitose Feb 2. Pegasis can use Air Canada's new Sapporo–Vancouver nonstop (AC54, Tue/Fri/Sun), and Aoki can use Spring or China Eastern nonstop to Shanghai.
why: No flight back to Tokyo or Osaka on the last day, and Tue Feb 2 is exactly an AC54 day.
cost: Google Flights snapshot on Sep 25, 2026, one way: CTS→Toronto via Vancouver (Air Canada) from ¥80,050; CTS→Shanghai Pudong nonstop Spring 13:50→17:00 ¥83,340 on Feb 2 (¥46,950 on Feb 1), China Eastern 13:30 nonstop; for comparison KIX→PVG Spring from ¥34,200 and NRT→PVG Spring ¥46,460 on Feb 2. Round trips / multi-city can be cheaper; check.
winterNote: Air Canada YVR–CTS runs Dec 17, 2026 – Mar 26, 2027, B787: AC55 YVR 13:25 → CTS 15:35+1 (Mon/Thu/Sat), AC54 CTS 19:55 → YVR 11:10 (Tue/Fri/Sun); Google Flights showed 19:35 departure for Feb 2, so check. Chinese New Year is Feb 6, 2027, so China flights around Feb 1–5 cost more; book early. CTS flights can be delayed by snowstorms: sleep in Sapporo on D14, not Niseko.

experience.hook: End the trip at the snow airport, with a nonstop home for both.
moments: Eat a last ramen at New Chitose's Ramen Dojo while Aoki boards the 13:50 Shanghai flight.
Buy Royce chocolate and Shiroi Koibito in the domestic terminal before Pegasis checks in.
Board the Air Canada 787 in the evening and land in Vancouver the same morning.
experience.tip: Search Aoki's CTS→PVG for Feb 1 and Feb 2: it was about ¥36,000 cheaper on Feb 1.

title: Hokkaido: 4 days or 7?
titleJa: 北海道は4日か7日か
summary: Versions A and B give Hokkaido 4 nights (fly Osaka→CTS on Fri Jan 29); version C gives 7 nights (fly Tue Jan 26). With 4 nights you get about 1.5 ski days; with 7 you get 3 ski days, Otaru, Sapporo and Asahikawa, but lose Nagoya/Numazu or the Alps.
why: Pegasis is a good skier and Aoki needs time to learn; the west side has most of the anime and car places.
cost: Each extra Hokkaido day with a car costs about ¥5,000–7,000 per person in car + fuel (approx), plus a Niseko lift ticket if skiing. The flight Osaka→CTS costs the same on either date (Jetstar/Peach ~¥7,000–10,000).
winterNote: No big Hokkaido festival falls inside the trip: Sapporo Snow Festival 2027 is Feb 4–11 and Otaru Snow Light Path Feb 6–13. So the Hokkaido part is for ski, snow scenery, onsen and food. Kansai side: Wakakusa Yamayaki Sat Jan 23 (only version C). Keep at least 1 buffer night in Sapporo before the flight home in case of snowstorms.

experience.hook: Choose: more towns in the west, or more powder in the north.
moments: Pick 4 days if Numazu, Ghibli, the car museum or Shirakawa-go matter most.
Pick 7 days if Pegasis wants 3 real powder days and Aoki wants to learn slowly.
Either way, sleep the last night in Sapporo, 40 min from the airport.
experience.tip: A middle option: fly on Wed Jan 27 (5 nights) by dropping one Kyoto day.

title: Grand Sumo New Year Tournament
titleJa: 大相撲一月場所（初場所）両国国技館
summary: The January Grand Sumo tournament runs Jan 10–24, 2027 at Ryogoku Kokugikan, so it is on during all Tokyo days. Go in the afternoon; the top-division bouts start at about 16:00 and end at 18:00.
why: It is only on 6 times a year in 3 cities, and your dates fall inside it by luck; it is a strong 'only in Japan' event for both of you.
cost: Chair seat 3,500–9,000 JPY weekday (C 3,500, B 5,000, A 8,000); box seat 8,500+ JPY; D seat 2,500 JPY
winterNote: Hatsu Basho 2027: Jan 10 (Sun) – Jan 24 (Sun). Advance tickets on sale Dec 5, 2026 (before the rankings are out). Jan 20–22 are weekdays (cheaper, easier). Jan 23 (Sat) and 24 (final day) sell out first.

experience.hook: Watch giant wrestlers slam together in two seconds, in a live 11,000-seat hall.
moments: Wait outside Ryogoku Kokugikan in the afternoon to see wrestlers walk in wearing kimono and hair topknots.
Eat the famous Kokugikan yakitori, made in the hall's own basement kitchen, from your seat.
Try a bowl of chanko nabe, the wrestlers' hot pot stew, sold in the basement.
Watch the top-division ring entry: wrestlers in silk aprons circle the ring, then the yokozuna does his stamping ritual.
Hear the crowd roar as wrestlers throw salt, stare each other down, and crash together.
experience.tip: Arrive around 14:00: lower-division bouts are quieter, and you can buy yakitori before the top bouts start near 16:00.

title: teamLab Planets and Toyosu footbath
titleJa: チームラボプラネッツ TOKYO DMM／豊洲 千客万来
summary: teamLab Planets is a digital art museum where you walk barefoot through water and light rooms. Next door, Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai has free rooftop footbaths with a view over Tokyo Bay, and a 24 h onsen (Manyo Club).
why: It is one of the top-ranked Tokyo spots on Xiaohongshu and Japanese blogs, and the onsen next door gives a first soak after the long flight.
cost: teamLab approx 3,600–4,800 JPY (price changes by date); footbath free; Manyo Club onsen 3,850 JPY + 150 JPY bath tax
winterNote: Indoor. teamLab Planets is extended to end of 2027. Manyo Club is open 24 h (bath closed 3:00–5:00); footbath garden 9:00–22:00. Book teamLab time slot in advance.

places.ja: チームラボプラネッツ

experience.hook: Walk barefoot through knee-deep water full of glowing digital koi.
moments: Take off your shoes, lock them away, and roll your trousers above the knee.
Wade through warm water while light koi swim around your legs and burst into flowers.
Lie back under the dome where flowers fall and spin above you.
Stand inside the Infinite Crystal Universe, a mirror room of hanging LED strings.
Walk to Toyosu Senkyaku Banrai and dip your feet in the free rooftop footbath over Tokyo Bay.
experience.tip: Wear shorts or loose trousers. After, soak at Manyo Club next door, with hot spring water trucked in from Hakone.

title: Asakusa, Skytree and Yanaka old town
titleJa: 浅草寺・東京スカイツリー・谷中銀座
summary: Walk Senso-ji temple and Nakamise street in Asakusa, then see Tokyo Skytree across the river. Yanaka Ginza is a small old shopping street with snacks and cats, 'old Tokyo' feeling.
why: Asakusa is the top 'old Japan' spot for Chinese and Japanese visitors, and it is close to Ryogoku (sumo) and Kinshicho (day 2).
cost: Temple free; Skytree deck approx 2,000–3,500 JPY (check); snacks 1,000–2,000 JPY
winterNote: Open all year. Winter air is clear, so the Skytree has the best chance of a Mt Fuji view in the morning.

experience.hook: Old Tokyo temple smoke in the morning, the city from 350 m by afternoon.
moments: Walk under the giant red lantern of Kaminarimon gate to Senso-ji temple.
Wave incense smoke over your head at the big burner in front of the main hall, for good health.
Eat warm ningyo-yaki cakes and fried age-manju on Nakamise street.
Ride up Tokyo Skytree and look for Mt Fuji in the clear winter sky.
Walk down the Yuyake Dandan steps into Yanaka Ginza and eat a hot menchi-katsu.
experience.tip: Reach Senso-ji before 9:00 for photos with no crowds; Nakamise shops open later, so come back for snacks.

title: Tsukiji breakfast, Tsukishima monja
titleJa: 築地場外市場・月島もんじゃストリート
summary: Eat seafood bowls, tamagoyaki and grilled oysters at Tsukiji Outer Market in the morning. In the evening, cook monjayaki yourself on a hot plate on Tsukishima's monja street (70+ shops).
why: Chinese guides list both as must-eat Tokyo food, and both are cheap and fun for two people.
cost: Tsukiji 2,000–4,000 JPY; monja 1,500–3,000 JPY
winterNote: Tsukiji shops open early morning and many close by early afternoon; some close on Sundays and Wednesdays (check shop). Jan 20 is a Wednesday.

places.ja: 月島もんじゃストリート

experience.hook: Raw tuna for breakfast, then cook your own messy Tokyo pancake at night.
moments: Walk the narrow lanes of Tsukiji Outer Market while it is still cold and busy.
Eat sweet tamagoyaki on a stick and a grilled scallop hot off the fire.
Share a kaisendon bowl piled with tuna, salmon roe and uni.
At night on Tsukishima monja street, fry cabbage in a ring on the hot plate, then pour the batter inside.
Scrape crispy monja off the iron with a tiny spatula; try mentaiko, mochi and cheese.
experience.tip: Go to Tsukiji by 8:00 or 9:00. At the monja shop, ask the staff to cook the first one so you learn.

title: Shinjuku yakitori alleys and Golden Gai
titleJa: 思い出横丁・新宿ゴールデン街
summary: Eat yakitori and drink in the small smoky shops of Omoide Yokocho, then go to Golden Gai, 200 tiny bars in 6 narrow lanes. Both are a short walk from your Shinjuku hotel.
why: Easy first-night or last-night plan near the hotel, with no transport needed.
cost: 3,000–6,000 JPY; many Golden Gai bars charge a seat fee of 500–1,500 JPY
winterNote: Open all year, evenings. Some bars do not accept tourists or charge a cover; look for signs at the door.

experience.hook: Yakitori smoke, tiny bars with six seats, and Showa-era Tokyo alleys.
moments: Squeeze onto a stool in Omoide Yokocho and order skewers straight from the charcoal grill.
Drink a cold beer or highball while smoke drifts under the red lanterns.
Walk to Golden Gai and look through its six narrow lanes of tiny bars.
Pick a bar with an English sign, climb the steep stairs, and talk with the bartender and strangers.
experience.tip: Check the sign on each door for the seat fee. Have one drink per bar and move on to see several.

title: Tokyo public bath and sauna
titleJa: 黄金湯（墨田区）／小杉湯（高円寺）
summary: A sento is a local public bath. Koganeyu near Kinshicho is a modern sento with a very hot sauna and cold plunge; Kosugiyu in Koenji is a 1933 wooden bath with a Mt Fuji wall painting.
why: Koganeyu is 6 min from Kinshicho, already on day 2, so it is a cheap real Tokyo onsen-style end to the anime day.
cost: Bath 550 JPY; Koganeyu sauna +350–600 JPY
winterNote: Open all year. Check the weekly closing day on each official site before you go. Towels can be rented.
photoQuery: sento public bath Tokyo Mount Fuji mural

experience.hook: Hot sauna, ice-cold plunge, then craft beer while a DJ plays vinyl.
moments: Buy your ticket at the Koganeyu machine, near Kinshicho, and rent a towel.
Sweat in the wood sauna, then drop into the cold plunge. Repeat three times.
Soak in the high-carbonated bath and feel small bubbles cover your skin.
Sit at the bar counter by reception with a craft beer while the DJ plays records.
Or go to Kosugiyu in Koenji for its white milk bath under a painted Mt Fuji.
experience.tip: Wash fully before you enter any bath and keep the small towel out of the water. Weekday evenings are quieter.

title: Shibuya Nintendo, Pokemon and Harajuku
titleJa: 渋谷PARCO（Nintendo TOKYO・ポケモンセンターシブヤ）・竹下通り・明治神宮
summary: Before Shibuya Sky, visit Nintendo TOKYO and Pokemon Center Shibuya, both in Shibuya PARCO, plus Don Quijote and GiGO arcades nearby. Walk to Harajuku Takeshita Street and the quiet Meiji Jingu forest shrine.
why: It fills the day 5 afternoon near Shibuya Sky with game shops, arcades and a big shrine in one walk.
cost: Free entry; shopping budget
winterNote: All indoor except the shrine. Weekends (Jan 23 is Saturday) are very crowded at PARCO.

experience.hook: Nintendo, Pokemon and arcades in one building, then a quiet forest shrine.
moments: Browse Nintendo TOKYO in Shibuya PARCO for Mario and Zelda goods you cannot buy outside Japan.
See the life-size Mewtwo in its glass tank at Pokemon Center Shibuya, same floor.
Cross the Shibuya Scramble with thousands of people when all lights turn green.
Eat a crepe on crowded Takeshita Street in Harajuku.
Walk under the tall wooden torii into the silent Meiji Jingu forest and see the wall of sake barrels.
experience.tip: Book Shibuya Sky for about 30 minutes before sunset (near 17:00 in late January) to see day, sunset and night.

title: Yokohama Chinatown and Cup Noodles
titleJa: 横浜中華街・カップヌードルミュージアム横浜・赤レンガ倉庫
summary: Make your own Cup Noodle at the Cup Noodles Museum, walk the Red Brick Warehouse and Osanbashi pier, then eat in Chinatown. Minato Mirai is lit at night across the water.
why: Yokohama is next to Kawasaki and Daikoku PA, so it fits the day 3 afternoon before the car meet at night.
cost: Museum 500 JPY + My Cup Noodle 500 JPY; food 2,000–4,000 JPY
winterNote: Cup Noodles Museum is closed on Tuesdays (Jan 19 is Tuesday; Jan 21 Thursday is fine). Open 10:00–18:00, last entry 17:00.

places.ja: カップヌードルミュージアム横浜

experience.hook: Design your own Cup Noodle, then eat soup dumplings in Japan's biggest Chinatown.
moments: Draw your own design on a blank cup at the Cup Noodles Museum, then pick one soup and four toppings.
Watch staff seal your noodles and blow up an air-bag package to carry home.
Walk the Red Brick Warehouse and look for the outdoor winter ice rink.
Eat hot xiaolongbao and pan-fried shengjianbao on the street in Chinatown.
Stand on Osanbashi pier at night and see the Minato Mirai Ferris wheel lights over the water.
experience.tip: Get your My Cup Noodles Factory ticket first thing when you arrive; slots can fill on busy days.

title: Nikko shrines and frozen falls
titleJa: 日光東照宮・華厳滝・中禅寺湖
summary: Take the Tobu train from Asakusa to Nikko to see the gold Toshogu shrine in snow. Then take the bus up to Kegon Falls and Lake Chuzenji, where the small side falls freeze into ice.
why: A snowy World Heritage shrine and ice falls in one day from Tokyo, a good first taste of winter before Zao.
cost: Approx 6,000–9,000 JPY (train, bus, shrine, Kegon elevator); Tobu NIKKO PASS options (World Heritage Area 3,000 JPY; Oku-Nikko needs the ALL AREA pass, check price)
winterNote: The 12 small falls (十二滝) around Kegon usually freeze late Jan – early Feb; the main fall keeps flowing. Akechidaira Ropeway is closed Jan 16, 2026 – Aug 31, 2027. Irohazaka road can be icy; bus is safer.

experience.hook: A gold shrine under snow, and a 97 m waterfall with frozen side falls.
moments: Ride the Tobu express from Asakusa and watch the land turn white near Nikko.
Walk to the red Shinkyo bridge standing over a cold, fast river.
Find the Three Wise Monkeys, the Sleeping Cat, and the gold Yomeimon gate at Toshogu.
Take the elevator down to the Kegon Falls deck and see the ice beside the falling water.
Eat hot yuba (tofu skin), a Nikko special, to warm up.
experience.tip: Reach Toshogu near opening time, before tour groups. Take the bus up the Irohazaka road; it is icy for drivers.

title: Mt Takao winter Fuji view
titleJa: 高尾山
summary: An easy mountain 50 minutes from Shinjuku by Keio train. Take the cable car halfway, walk past Yakuo-in temple to the top (599 m) and see Mt Fuji on a clear morning.
why: Cheap, short, easy for both, and winter is the clearest season for the Fuji view from the top.
cost: Train approx 400 JPY each way; cable car 490 JPY one-way / 980 JPY return
winterNote: Open all year; the path can be icy in the morning after snow. Go early for the clearest Fuji view.
photoQuery: Mount Takao summit Mount Fuji view

experience.hook: A short climb from Shinjuku to a clear view of snowy Mt Fuji.
moments: Ride the Keio line from Shinjuku to Takaosanguchi, about 50 minutes.
Take Japan's steepest cable car up to the halfway station in 6 minutes.
Walk past the Octopus Cedar and the tengu statues at Yakuo-in temple.
Stand on the 599 m summit and see Mt Fuji white against the blue sky.
Eat a bowl of tororo soba with grated mountain yam at the bottom.
experience.tip: Start before 9:00, since Fuji is clearest in the morning. Soak at Gokurakuyu onsen next to Takaosanguchi station after.

title: Kawagoe Little Edo old town
titleJa: 小江戸川越（時の鐘・菓子屋横丁）
summary: Kawagoe has old black clay warehouse streets, the wooden Toki no Kane bell tower and a candy alley. It is about 30 minutes by train from Ikebukuro.
why: An easy half day of 'Edo period' Japan with street food, without a long trip.
cost: Train approx 1,000 JPY return; food 1,000–2,000 JPY
winterNote: Open all year, outdoor walking; shops close around 17:00.

experience.hook: Walk Edo-period warehouse streets and eat sweet potato everything.
moments: Walk the Kurazukuri street of black clay warehouses built after a big fire in 1893.
Stand under the wooden Toki no Kane bell tower and hear it ring.
Buy old-style candy and a very long brown sugar fugashi stick in Kashiya Yokocho.
Eat Kawagoe's famous sweet potato as chips, soft-serve or warm roasted.
Try a COEDO craft beer, the local Kawagoe brewery.
experience.tip: The bell rings at 6:00, 12:00, 15:00 and 18:00: be at the tower at 15:00. Shops close near 17:00.
